checklist.step: Declare the incident against the UK regulated entity and open the incident record
actions: In ServiceNow open Incident ▸ Major Incident and set Priority = P1/P2, Legal Entity = the UK Solvency UK entity, and Detection Time to the first alert timestamp from the monitoring tool, not the time the bridge was opened.

Record in the Description: what failed, which important business services are affected, the customer-facing symptom, and whether policyholder payments, claims settlement or annuity payroll are interrupted.
Add the standing PRA-notification watchers — Operational Risk Manager, Head of Compliance, Chief Risk Officer — to the incident so the 4-hour clock is visible to them from declaration.
Open the incident chronology worksheet and start logging every decision with a UTC timestamp and named decision-maker.
checklist.done: a P1/P2 record exists against the UK entity with detection time, affected services and the notification watchers attached, and a timestamped chronology is running.

checklist.step: Test the outage against the important business service impact tolerances
actions: Open the firm's SS1/21 important business service register and identify every service the failed component supports (annuity payment, claims settlement, new business issue, policyholder servicing).

For each affected service read the board-approved impact tolerance — the maximum tolerable disruption expressed in hours plus the volume/harm metric — and compare it to elapsed outage time and transactions queued.
Ask the Business Continuity Manager for the count of unpaid annuity instalments, unsettled claims and failed premium collections accumulated so far and record them on the assessment.
Record a breached / at-risk / within-tolerance verdict per service with the elapsed hours and the tolerance figure side by side.
Hand the verdict to the Operational Risk Manager within 2 hours of declaration — a breached tolerance presumptively triggers PRA notification.
checklist.done: each affected important business service has a written within/at-risk/breached verdict with elapsed hours against the board-approved tolerance.

checklist.step: Quantify the solvency, own-funds and policyholder impact of the event
actions: Estimate the direct loss (remediation cost, redress, penalty exposure, unrecoverable reinsurance) and pass it to the Valuation Actuary for an own-funds effect.
Run an off-cycle SCR coverage estimate in the capital model reflecting the loss against basic own funds and any operational-risk capital add-on the event implies.
State the estimated movement in the SCR coverage ratio in percentage points and whether it crosses any risk-appetite trigger in the capital ladder.
Write the figures onto the materiality assessment — a material solvency, governance, risk-profile or reporting effect is exactly what Reporting 2 tests.
checklist.done: the assessment carries an estimated direct loss, the own-funds effect and the SCR coverage movement in percentage points.

checklist.step: Test the event against the PRA Reporting 2 predefined-event list
actions: Open the dated copy of PRA Rulebook Reporting 2 and walk the predefined-event list line by line: material effect on solvency, on the system of governance, on the risk profile, on the firm's ability to report; failure of a material reinsurance arrangement; breach of obligations to policyholders; significant change in governance or SMF holders.
Mark each line Yes / No / Not yet determinable and write one sentence of reasoning citing the facts and figures already gathered, never a bare 'No'.
Where any line is Yes or Not yet determinable, set the assessment outcome to NOTIFIABLE and start drafting rather than waiting for certainty.
Attach the dated rulebook PDF to the incident record so the version relied on is provable.
checklist.done: every predefined-event line has a Yes/No/undetermined answer with reasoning, and a NOTIFIABLE / NOT NOTIFIABLE outcome is written.

checklist.step: Establish whether a material outsourcer or ICT third party caused or amplified the event
actions: Open the outsourcing and third-party register maintained under SS2/21 and identify whether the failed component sits with a material outsourcer or an important-business-service-supporting ICT provider.

Pull the contract's incident-notification clause, agreed RTO/RPO and step-in rights from the contract lifecycle management repository and confirm the provider notified the firm inside the contractual window.
Demand from the provider a written incident statement covering root cause, affected tenants, data exposure and restoration ETA, and attach it to the incident record.
Tell the Operational Risk Manager whether the register entry itself needs updating — a material outsourcing failure is separately notifiable to the PRA.
checklist.done: the provider is identified against the outsourcing register, its written incident statement is attached, and the contractual notification timing is evidenced.

checklist.step: Determine the cyber, data and confidentiality dimension of the incident
actions: Have the SOC Lead pull the SIEM correlation timeline for the affected estate — authentication anomalies, data egress volumes, privileged account use — for the 72 hours before detection.
State in writing whether policyholder personal data or confidential regulatory data was accessed, exfiltrated or rendered unavailable, and quantify the record count.
Where personal data is involved, hand the finding to the Data Protection Officer for the separate ICO 72-hour assessment and record the handover time.

Confirm whether the firm's regulatory reporting systems (BEEDS submission chain, the actuarial model, the general ledger) are compromised or unavailable — inability to report is itself a Reporting 2 predefined event.
checklist.done: a written data-impact statement exists with record counts, the DPO handover is timestamped, and the availability of the regulatory reporting chain is stated.

checklist.step: Obtain the Chief Risk Officer's materiality decision inside four hours of declaration
actions: Convene the notification call with the Operational Risk Manager, Operational Resilience Lead, Head of Capital Management and Head of Compliance no later than 3 hours after P1 declaration.
Read the impact-tolerance verdict, the SCR coverage movement, the third-party statement and the Reporting 2 line-by-line assessment before deciding.

Record NOTIFY or DO NOT NOTIFY with named reasons on the assessment and sign it — a DO NOT NOTIFY on an impact-tolerance breach must state explicitly why the breach is immaterial to solvency, governance, risk profile and reporting.
Where the position is uncertain, decide to notify: Fundamental Rule 7 is not satisfied by waiting for the full picture.
Set the interim-update cadence (default 48 hours) and name the single point of contact for the PRA supervisor.
checklist.done: a signed, timed CRO decision exists inside 4 hours of declaration, with reasons and a named supervisory point of contact.

checklist.step: Draft the PRA notification pack
actions: Open the three-part notification template and complete Part A: legal entity name and FRN, incident reference, detection and declaration times in UTC, current status, and a factual chronology with no speculation.

Complete Part B: important business services affected and the tolerance breached, policyholder harm quantified (payments missed, claims delayed, customers affected), estimated own-funds and SCR coverage impact, and the Reporting 2 limb relied on.
Complete Part C: containment actions taken, workarounds live, restoration ETA, third-party involvement and the interim-update cadence the firm commits to.
State plainly what is not yet known and when the firm will know it — the PRA reads silence as concealment.
Circulate the draft to the CRO and Head of Compliance for comment with a fixed 60-minute turnaround.
checklist.done: a completed three-part notification exists with quantified impact, the cited Reporting 2 limb, and an explicit list of open unknowns.

checklist.step: Clear the notification through Regulatory Counsel before it is sent
actions: Review the draft against Fundamental Rule 7 and the Reporting 2 limb cited, checking that no statement overstates certainty of root cause or understates policyholder harm.
Confirm the notification does not waive privilege over the forensic investigation and that any legally privileged material is referenced but not attached.
Confirm whether parallel notifications are owed to the FCA, the ICO or an overseas group supervisor and note them in the covering email.
Approve in writing on the incident record with name, role and timestamp, or return with tracked changes inside 60 minutes.
checklist.done: counsel approval is recorded with a timestamp on the incident record, or the returned changes are incorporated.

checklist.step: Send the notification to the PRA and capture the acknowledgement
actions: Send the notification to the firm's named PRA supervisory contact and the PRA supervision team mailbox, copying the CRO and the SMF holder accountable for the affected service, with the subject line 'Reporting 2 notification — <entity> — <incident ref> — <date>'.

Where the incident affects data submitted through the Bank of England BEEDS portal or will delay a scheduled QRT/NST submission, say so explicitly in the notification and copy the BEEDS firm administrator.
Save the sent item with full headers as a PDF into the incident record so the send timestamp is provable independent of the mail system.
Log the acknowledgement time when the supervisor replies, and chase at 24 hours if none arrives.
checklist.done: the notification is sent within 24 hours of declaration, the sent item with headers is filed, and acknowledgement (or a chase) is logged.

checklist.step: Fire the parallel notifications owed to other authorities
actions: Where the firm is dual-regulated and the incident affects consumers or market integrity, file the FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15 through the FCA Connect portal and record the reference.
Where personal data was breached, confirm the Data Protection Officer has assessed reportability and, if reportable, filed with the ICO inside 72 hours of awareness; record the ICO case reference.
Where a group or overseas supervisor has an equivalent obligation, notify through the group regulatory affairs contact and log the date and recipient.
Record every parallel notification on one row of the incident record so the firm can prove a consistent account was given to each authority.
checklist.done: each applicable authority notification is filed with its reference number and the accounts given are consistent.

checklist.step: Issue interim updates on the committed cadence until the incident closes
actions: Every 48 hours, or immediately on a material change of facts, send an update restating status, revised restoration ETA, revised policyholder-harm figures and any change to the estimated own-funds impact.
Correct in writing anything stated in an earlier update that has turned out to be wrong, calling out the correction explicitly rather than silently restating.
Where a workaround has become the operating model, say for how long the firm intends to run it and what the residual risk is.
File each update in the incident record and tick the reminder task in the GRC incident register so the cadence is auditable.
checklist.done: updates exist at no more than 48-hour intervals from notification to closure, with any earlier misstatement expressly corrected.

checklist.step: Restore service and record actual disruption against the tolerance
actions: Confirm with the service owners that each important business service is delivering end-to-end, not merely that the infrastructure is up, and record the restoration time in UTC.
Compute actual disruption duration per service and compare it to the board-approved impact tolerance; record the overrun in hours where breached.
Reconcile the backlog cleared — annuity instalments paid late, claims settled late, premiums collected late — and pass the counts to the Complaints Manager for redress assessment.
Confirm no data loss beyond the agreed RPO by reconciling policy and payment record counts before and after recovery with the Data Quality Analyst.
checklist.done: restoration times, actual-versus-tolerance overruns and cleared backlog counts are recorded and reconciled to record counts.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review and file the closure report with the PRA
actions: Hold the post-incident review within 10 business days of restoration with the incident lead, service owners, the third party where involved and the Operational Risk Manager.
Establish root cause using the forensic timeline, distinguishing the trigger from the control failures that let it spread, and name each failed control with its owner.
Write the closure report: final chronology, actual versus tolerated disruption, final policyholder-harm and financial figures, root cause, and a dated remediation plan with named owners.
Send the closure report to the PRA supervisory contact within 20 business days of restoration and file the acknowledgement.
Load each remediation action into the GRC platform with a due date and a control owner so the plan is tracked, not just written.
checklist.done: a closure report with root cause and a dated, owned remediation plan is with the PRA within 20 business days and the actions are tracked in GRC.

checklist.step: Retain the evidence and feed the event into operational risk capital and the ORSA
actions: Move the complete incident bundle — chronology, materiality assessment, CRO decision, notification as sent, interim updates, closure report, acknowledgements — into the compliance evidence repository indexed by entity, incident reference and date.
Apply the 10-year-from-closure retention label so the record survives beyond the usual document lifecycle.
Book the realised loss into the operational risk loss database with Basel-style event-type and business-line coding so it feeds next cycle's operational risk capital assessment.
Give the Risk Management team the event summary for inclusion in the ORSA operational risk section and, where the loss is severe, as a candidate reverse stress scenario.
checklist.done: the bundle is filed with a 10-year retention label, the loss is coded into the loss database, and the event is handed to the ORSA authors.

testing.step: Build the complete population of potentially notifiable events for the period
actions: Extract from ServiceNow every incident with Priority P1 or P2, Legal Entity = the UK Solvency UK entity, and detection date inside the six-month test window, with detection, declaration and restoration timestamps.
Add from the GRC platform every recorded impact-tolerance breach, material outsourcer failure, reinsurance counterparty default or downgrade, and SMF/board change in the same window.
Add from the operational risk loss database every loss booked above the notification-assessment threshold, so events managed outside the ITSM tool cannot hide.
De-duplicate on incident reference and record the population count, extract date and query parameters in the workpaper.
testing.done: a de-duplicated population exists from three independent sources with the extract parameters and count documented.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record and prove completeness
actions: Reconcile the ITSM extract count to the monthly major-incident reports tabled at the Operational Risk Committee and explain every difference in writing.
Reconcile the impact-tolerance breach list to the resilience self-assessment monitoring pack and to service-availability data from the monitoring platform.
Test for suppressed severity by listing incidents downgraded from P1 to P2/P3 after declaration and confirming a documented reason exists for each downgrade.
Have the extract owner sign the population as complete and accurate before any sampling begins.
testing.done: the population reconciles to committee reporting and monitoring data, downgrades are explained, and completeness is signed.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of impact-tolerance breaches, reinsurance counterparty failures and incidents affecting the regulatory reporting chain.
Take 20 further incidents from the remaining population using a seeded random selection, with a minimum overall sample of 30 items.
Record the seed, population size, stratum boundaries and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically by a third party.
Include every incident where the recorded outcome was NOT NOTIFIABLE but an impact tolerance was at risk — the judgement calls are where the risk sits.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample is drawn with seed and strata documented and full coverage of the mandatory strata.

testing.step: Re-perform the Reporting 2 materiality assessment independently
actions: For each sampled incident, read the chronology, resilience verdict and financial impact but not the firm's assessment, and walk the PRA Rulebook Reporting 2 predefined-event list yourself.
Reach your own NOTIFIABLE / NOT NOTIFIABLE conclusion, citing the limb and the facts you relied on, then compare it to the firm's recorded outcome.
Treat as an exception any difference in outcome and any case where the right outcome rests on the wrong limb or on no cited limb at all.
Confirm the rulebook version relied on by the firm was the one in force on the incident date by opening the attached dated PDF.
testing.done: each sampled incident carries an independent re-performed conclusion with cited limb, compared to the firm's outcome.

testing.step: Trace notified events to the notification actually sent and its identifiers
actions: For every sampled NOTIFIABLE incident, open the filed sent item with headers and confirm recipient, subject line, incident reference and send timestamp.
Confirm the notification content matches the incident record on the material facts — services affected, tolerance breached, policyholder harm figures, estimated own-funds impact.
Confirm the PRA acknowledgement is filed, or that a chase was raised at 24 hours where none was received.
Trace parallel FCA / ICO / group notifications to their reference numbers and confirm the accounts given are consistent with the PRA notification.
testing.done: each notified incident traces to a filed, timestamped notification with matching facts, acknowledgement and consistent parallel filings.

testing.step: Recompute the notification and reporting clocks
actions: Recompute elapsed hours from P1 declaration to notification send for every notified incident and test against the 24-hour standard.
Recompute elapsed hours from declaration to CRO materiality decision and test against the 4-hour standard, using the signed decision timestamp not the meeting invite.
Recompute the interval between consecutive interim updates and flag every gap exceeding 48 hours while the incident was open.
Recompute the business days from restoration to closure-report send and test against the 20-business-day standard using the England and Wales bank holiday calendar.
testing.done: all four clocks are recomputed per incident with breaches quantified in hours or business days.

testing.step: Re-derive the impact-tolerance verdict from raw monitoring data
actions: For each sampled incident, pull raw service-availability and transaction-throughput data from the monitoring platform for the incident window rather than relying on the incident record's stated duration.
Recompute actual disruption per important business service end to end, including degraded-service periods and manual workaround periods, not just the hard outage.
Compare the recomputed duration to the board-approved impact tolerance in force on that date and restate the verdict.
Flag every incident where the firm's recorded 'within tolerance' verdict does not survive the recomputation — those are unnotified breaches.
testing.done: each sampled incident has a monitoring-data-derived disruption duration and a restated tolerance verdict.

testing.step: Test the solvency impact figures back to the capital model and ledger
actions: For each notified incident claiming an SCR coverage impact, re-run the off-cycle estimate from the archived model point set and compare the coverage movement to the figure notified to the PRA.
Agree the direct loss quoted in the notification to the amount subsequently booked in the general ledger and to the operational risk loss database entry.
Where the notified impact proved materially wrong and was never corrected in an interim update, raise it as an accuracy exception under Fundamental Rule 7.
Confirm losses above the operational risk capital assessment threshold were carried into the next SCR operational risk module input.
testing.done: notified solvency impacts reconcile to the re-run model and the booked loss, and uncorrected misstatements are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception carrying the incident reference, the standard missed (non-notification, late notification, no CRO decision, missed update cadence, misstated impact) and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — triage missed the entity, materiality call not escalated, tolerance data unavailable, template not completed, ownership vacancy — and name an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any unnotified material event, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the Chief Risk Officer within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, root cause, named owner, remediation date and, where material, an opened self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Compute the exception rate by stratum and compare it to the zero-non-notification and one-late-notification thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with a direct reference to the workpaper evidence supporting each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled materiality assessment and sits outside operational risk, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, open breaches and self-report decisions to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate by stratum and a Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns production of the SCR and MCR for the UK solo entity each quarter and year-end, including the standard formula / internal model split and the risk margin under the Solvency II Reform Instrument 2024; reports the result to the CFO and the Board Risk Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Solvency Capital Requirement (General Provisions) 3 for the 99.5% one-year VaR calibration, the Solvency II (Reform) Instrument 2024 for the reduced risk margin and cost-of-capital, and Minimum Capital Requirement 2-4 for the 25%-45% corridor and the absolute MCR floor; each re-read at the start of every year-end cycle

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and annual capital production for the UK Solvency UK entity: data extract and validation -> best estimate liability and matching adjustment run -> risk margin -> standard formula modules and correlation aggregation (or approved internal model) -> LACDT/LACTP -> SCR, MCR and own-funds tiering -> sign-off, covering all annuity and life business

In-scope systems.value: The valuation and capital model holds the model points, the stressed runs and the aggregation; asset data comes from the investment book of record and own funds from the general ledger; the run version and its inputs are locked in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: SCR/MCR Production and Calculation Manual — module-by-module method (interest rate, equity with symmetric adjustment, property, spread, currency, concentration, counterparty default type 1/2, life underwriting, expense, catastrophe, operational risk), correlation matrices, LACDT method and the MCR corridor test

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Model Risk Manager under the technical actuarial standards, with the model change policy approved by the Board; re-approved annually and on every PRA-notified major model change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly SCR/MCR must be complete for the S.25 and S.28 templates in time for the 30-business-day solo quarterly submission under PS15/24; annual SCR/MCR for the 70-business-day annual submission; the matching adjustment attestation is due annually within the PRA-specified window

Deadline reminders configured.value: The capital production calendar sets working-day milestones back from the 30/70-business-day submission dates — data cut WD+3, model run WD+8, review WD+12, sign-off WD+18 — with automated alerts to each owner and an amber flag at 2 days of slippage

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Locked model run version, input data extracts with hash, module-by-module results, aggregation workings, validation report, expert judgement log and the signed sign-off memo retained 10 years from the reference date in the model governance repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Model errors, unapproved methodology deviations, failed validation checks and post-submission restatements are logged as capital-production issues with root cause, materiality in coverage-ratio percentage points and a dated fix

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs the SCR/MCR result and every methodology change or error correction affecting the reported coverage ratio, countersigned by the Chief Financial Officer as the accountable SMF

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every SCR and MCR calculation produced for the UK entity in the year — four quarterly runs plus the annual run — together with the underlying module results, model change records and expert judgements applied in each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Independent recalculation must agree the SCR to within 0.5% and the MCR to the pound; any module recalculation differing by more than 1% of that module, any breach of the 25%-45% MCR corridor left unhandled, or any unapproved methodology change is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly with a full annual calculation; independent validation runs on 100% of the annual calculation and on one selected quarter, with analytical review of the remaining quarters

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Second-line model risk review, independent of the capital production team, supported by Internal Audit; no reviewer may have built, parameterised or run the calculation under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual SCR validation report and quarterly validation memos (data checks, recalculation of each module, movement analysis, expert judgement challenge, exceptions) held in the model governance repository and cross-linked to the BEEDS submission pack

Regulator-ready documentation.value: SCR calculation documentation, validation report, model change log, expert judgement register and the S.25/S.28 templates as submitted, presentable to a PRA supervisory or internal model review within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Financial Officer owns PRA capital queries; the Chief Actuary answers technical method challenge and any request under the internal model or matching adjustment permissions, with responses cleared by the Chief Risk Officer before issue

checklist.step: Open the capital production cycle and lock the reference date basis
actions: Open the capital production calendar for the reference date and confirm the working-day milestones back from the PS15/24 deadline — 30 business days for a quarter end, 70 business days for 31 December.
Confirm with the Chief Actuary which basis applies: standard formula, the PRA-approved internal model, or partial internal model by module, and record the permission reference for each.

List the permissions in force at the reference date — matching adjustment portfolios, volatility adjustment, transitional measure on technical provisions (TMTP), undertaking-specific parameters — and attach the PRA approval letters.
Circulate the milestone plan to the Valuation Actuary, ALM actuary, Controller and Regulatory Reporting Manager with named owners per milestone.
checklist.done: the cycle is open with a working-day plan tied to the 30/70-business-day deadline and every permission in force is listed with its approval letter.

checklist.step: Extract and validate the policy, asset and reinsurance data feeding the calculation
actions: Extract the in-force policy file at the reference date from the policy administration system — annuity in payment, deferred annuity and life records with sums assured, annuity amounts, ages, guarantee periods and escalation.

Extract the asset file from the investment book of record with CUSIP/ISIN, market value, credit rating, duration, sector and matching-adjustment portfolio tag, and the reinsurance recoverable file from the reinsurance administration system.

Run the data quality suite for completeness, accuracy and appropriateness: record-count reconciliation to the policy admin control totals, annuity payroll reconciliation to the ledger, null and out-of-range checks on age, rating and duration.

Reconcile total asset market value to the general ledger investment balance and total technical provision inputs to the prior quarter roll-forward, explaining every difference above the agreed tolerance.
Sign the data quality report and hand the locked extract, with its hash, to the Valuation Actuary — the calculation may not start on unsigned data.
checklist.done: policy, asset and reinsurance extracts are reconciled to the ledger and admin control totals, the DQ report is signed, and the locked extract hash is recorded.

checklist.step: Value the technical provisions as the starting balance sheet for the SCR
actions: Load the locked data into the valuation model and run the best estimate liability on the reference-date basis using the current demographic and expense assumptions signed off by the Chief Actuary.

Apply the reference-date risk-free term structure published by the PRA/Bank of England, with the matching adjustment applied only to the approved MA portfolios and the fundamental spread deducted per portfolio.
Confirm the MA portfolio still passes the eligibility tests — cash flow matching within tolerance, no forced-sale assumption, ring-fenced asset identification — and record the test results.
Produce the Solvency UK balance sheet: assets at market value, best estimate liability, risk margin placeholder and the resulting excess of assets over liabilities feeding basic own funds.
checklist.done: a reference-date best estimate liability exists on the approved basis with MA eligibility evidenced and a balance sheet handed to the capital team.

checklist.step: Run the market risk module stresses
actions: Run the interest rate up and down stresses on the prescribed relative shocks by term, revaluing assets and liabilities together, and take the more onerous direction as the module result.

Run the equity stress on type 1 and type 2 holdings applying the symmetric adjustment published for the reference date, the property stress, and the currency stress in both directions for every material non-sterling exposure.

Run the spread stress by credit quality step and duration across the bond, structured and loan portfolios, applying the MA-portfolio treatment where approved, and the concentration stress on exposures above the relevant threshold per counterparty.

Record each sub-module capital figure and aggregate them with the prescribed market-risk correlation matrix under both the interest-rate-up and interest-rate-down correlation sets, keeping the higher result.
Attach the asset positions driving the three largest sub-module results so the numbers can be explained to the Board and the PRA.
checklist.done: every market sub-module is run and aggregated under both correlation sets, with the driving exposures documented.

checklist.step: Run the counterparty default and life underwriting modules
actions: Build the type 1 exposure list — reinsurance recoverables net of collateral, derivative counterparties, cash at bank — with each counterparty's rating and loss-given-default, and compute the module using the prescribed variance and single-name concentration treatment.
Build the type 2 list — intermediary receivables and policyholder debtors past due more than three months — and apply the prescribed factors.

Run the life underwriting stresses: permanent mortality increase, permanent longevity reduction, disability-morbidity, mass lapse and level lapse up/down, expense (level and inflation), revision, and the life catastrophe absolute mortality uplift for the following year.
For an annuity-dominated book, evidence the longevity stress dominates and document the sensitivity of the module to the base mortality table and CMI improvement parameter used.
Aggregate the life sub-modules with the prescribed life correlation matrix and record each sub-module result on the results template.
checklist.done: counterparty type 1/2 and every life underwriting sub-module are computed and aggregated, with the longevity driver documented.

checklist.step: Compute the operational risk module and the loss-absorbing adjustments
actions: Compute the operational risk charge from earned premiums and technical provisions on the prescribed factors, apply the cap expressed as a percentage of the basic SCR, and add the unit-linked expense element where applicable.
Compute the loss-absorbing capacity of technical provisions (LACTP) only to the extent of future discretionary benefits genuinely reducible, and document the management actions relied on.
Compute the loss-absorbing capacity of deferred taxes (LACDT) and evidence recoverability against projected future taxable profits — an unsupportable LACDT is the single most common PRA challenge.
Have the Tax Manager confirm in writing the deferred tax position and the profit projections underpinning the LACDT credit claimed.
Record both adjustments as separate lines so the gross basic SCR and the net SCR are both visible.
checklist.done: operational risk, LACTP and LACDT are computed with written tax support for the LACDT and gross/net SCR shown separately.

checklist.step: Aggregate the modules into the basic SCR and the SCR
actions: Aggregate the market, counterparty default, life, health and non-life module results with the prescribed top-level correlation matrix to produce the basic SCR.

Add the operational risk charge and deduct LACTP and LACDT to produce the SCR, and check the result is expressed as the 99.5% one-year value-at-risk of basic own funds required by SCR General Provisions 3.
Where any ring-fenced fund or matching adjustment portfolio exists, compute its notional SCR separately and confirm no diversification benefit is taken across the ring fence.
Reconcile the aggregation workbook to the model output cell by cell and lock the workbook version alongside the model run in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the SCR is produced with a locked aggregation workbook, ring-fenced notional SCRs computed separately and no cross-fence diversification claimed.

checklist.step: Compute the risk margin under the Solvency II Reform Instrument 2024
actions: Project the SCR for non-hedgeable risks over the run-off of the in-force book, using the approved simplification and documenting why it is proportionate.
Apply the reformed cost-of-capital rate and the tapering factor introduced by the Solvency II (Reform) Instrument 2024, which materially reduces the life risk margin against the pre-reform basis.
Discount the projected cost-of-capital amounts on the reference-date risk-free curve and show the resulting risk margin against the prior period and against the pre-reform equivalent.
Feed the risk margin into the balance sheet as part of technical provisions and re-derive basic own funds accordingly.
checklist.done: the risk margin is computed on the reformed cost-of-capital and taper basis, discounted at the reference-date curve, and fed back into technical provisions.

checklist.step: Compute the MCR and test it against the corridor and the absolute floor
actions: Compute the linear MCR from the prescribed factors applied to technical provisions net of reinsurance and capital at risk by line of business.
Apply the corridor test under PRA Rulebook Minimum Capital Requirement 2-4: the MCR may be no lower than 25% and no higher than 45% of the SCR.
Compare the corridor result to the absolute minimum capital requirement floor applicable to the firm's permission type and take the higher figure.
Record which of the three constraints bound the result — linear, corridor or absolute floor — because that is what the S.28 template must show.
Hand the MCR and the binding constraint to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst for the S.28.01 template.
checklist.done: the MCR is computed, tested against the 25%-45% corridor and the absolute floor, and the binding constraint is named.

checklist.step: Determine own funds, tiering and eligibility to cover the SCR and MCR
actions: Derive basic own funds from the excess of assets over liabilities on the Solvency UK balance sheet, plus subordinated liabilities qualifying as own funds, less foreseeable dividends and distributions approved or proposed.

Classify each own-funds item into Tier 1 unrestricted, Tier 1 restricted, Tier 2 and Tier 3 by reference to its permanence, subordination and loss-absorbency features and the instrument's PRA approval where required.

Apply the eligibility limits — restricted Tier 1 capped as a share of total Tier 1, Tier 3 ineligible to cover the MCR, Tier 2 plus Tier 3 capped against the SCR — and show the ineligible amount separately.
Reconcile own funds to IFRS equity through a documented bridge so the Board and the auditors can follow the movement.
Confirm eligible own funds cover the SCR and the MCR at the reference date and state both coverage ratios to one decimal place.
checklist.done: own funds are tiered, eligibility limits applied, bridged to IFRS equity, and both coverage ratios are stated.

checklist.step: Run the movement analysis and explain the change since the prior reference date
actions: Build the SCR walk from prior period to current: new business, run-off, model and assumption changes, market movements by sub-module, data corrections and methodology changes, each as a separate step.
Build the own-funds walk: expected return, experience variances, assumption changes, market movements, capital actions and dividends.
Set a materiality threshold at 1 percentage point of coverage ratio and require a named owner and written explanation for every step above it.
Challenge any unexplained residual above the threshold with the module owner and re-run rather than plugging the difference.
checklist.done: SCR and own-funds walks reconcile to the reported figures with every step above 1 point of coverage explained and owned.

checklist.step: Record and challenge the expert judgements applied in the cycle
actions: List every expert judgement used — data proxies, approximation of missing attributes, simplifications in the risk margin projection, management actions in LACTP, LACDT recoverability, mapping of unrated assets to credit quality steps.
For each, record the alternative considered, the rationale, the quantified sensitivity to the SCR, and the date it was last challenged.
Present the judgements with material sensitivity to the Model Risk Manager for second-line challenge and record the outcome.
Retire judgements that have become unnecessary as data has improved rather than rolling them forward by default.
checklist.done: every expert judgement carries a rationale, a quantified SCR sensitivity and a dated second-line challenge outcome.

checklist.step: Route the calculation through model validation before sign-off
actions: Check the model version, parameter set and data extract hash used match those authorised under the model change policy and that no unapproved change entered the production run.
Re-perform an independent check of at least the market, life underwriting and operational risk modules, and recompute the top-level aggregation from the module results.
Run analytical review against the prior quarter and against the movement analysis, and challenge any module moving more than 10% without a named driver.
Write the validation report with a clear opinion, listing every finding with severity and a required-by date, and confirm whether any finding blocks sign-off.
checklist.done: a validation report with an opinion, an independent recomputation of the key modules and severity-rated findings exists before sign-off.

checklist.step: Sign off the SCR and MCR and release them to reporting
actions: Review the sign-off memo: SCR, MCR, eligible own funds by tier, both coverage ratios, movement analysis, validation opinion and open findings.
Confirm eligible own funds cover the SCR continuously through the period, not merely at the reference date, using the interim monitoring reports.
Sign as the accountable SMF alongside the Chief Actuary's technical sign-off, dating both signatures before the reporting pack is released.
Release the locked figures to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for the S.23.01 own funds, S.25 SCR and S.28 MCR templates and to the Board Risk Committee pack.
checklist.done: a dual-signed, dated sign-off memo exists and the locked figures are released to regulatory reporting and the Board pack.

checklist.step: Archive the run, the inputs and the documentation for the retention period
actions: Archive the locked model run, parameter set, input data extracts with hashes, module results, aggregation workbook, validation report and sign-off memo under the reference date.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the archive is retrievable by reference date, entity and module.
Record the run in the model change log with the version, the change made since the prior run and the approver.
Confirm the archived figures agree cell for cell with what was submitted through BEEDS once the submission is accepted.
checklist.done: a complete, hash-verified archive is retained for 10 years and agrees to the accepted BEEDS submission.

testing.step: Build the population of capital calculations and model changes for the year
actions: List every SCR and MCR production run for the UK entity in the year — four quarterly and one annual — with reference date, model version, run date and signatory.
Extract the model change log for the same period, including every parameter, assumption, data-mapping and code change, with its approval record.
Extract the expert judgement register and the open validation findings carried into each run.
Reconcile the run list to the figures actually submitted in the S.25 and S.28 templates for each reference date and resolve any run that has no submitted counterpart.
testing.done: a complete run and model-change population is built and reconciles to the submitted S.25/S.28 figures.

testing.step: Reconcile the calculation inputs to the source systems
actions: Agree total asset market value in the model input file to the investment book of record and to the general ledger investment balance at the reference date.
Agree the in-force policy count and total annuity in payment to the policy administration control totals and to the annuity payroll run for the reference month.
Agree reinsurance recoverables in the counterparty default input to the ceded accounting platform balances by counterparty.
Recompute the extract hash recorded in the archive against the archived file and confirm the data the model consumed is the data that was signed.
testing.done: asset, policy and reinsurance inputs agree to source systems and the archived extract hash verifies.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of modules and judgements to re-perform
actions: Take 100% of the annual reference-date calculation and one quarterly run selected at random with a recorded seed.
Within the selected runs take 100% of the market and life underwriting modules, the operational risk charge, LACDT, the risk margin and the MCR corridor test.
Take a random sample of 10 expert judgements weighted toward those with the largest quantified SCR sensitivity.
Record the seed, the selection date and the rationale for the stratification so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering the annual run, one quarter, the key modules and 10 weighted expert judgements is documented.

testing.step: Independently recalculate the market and life underwriting modules
actions: Rebuild the interest rate, equity, spread, property, currency and concentration stresses from the archived asset and liability data in an independent workbook, applying the prescribed shocks and the reference-date symmetric adjustment read from the published source.
Rebuild the longevity, mortality, lapse, expense and life catastrophe stresses from the archived model points and compare each sub-module to the production result.
Re-apply both interest-rate correlation sets and confirm the production run took the more onerous outcome.
Flag any sub-module differing by more than 1% and trace the difference to a specific input, parameter or code path before concluding.
testing.done: each sampled sub-module is independently rebuilt, compared within the 1% tolerance and every difference traced to a cause.

testing.step: Recompute the aggregation, the risk margin and the MCR corridor maths
actions: Re-perform the top-level correlation aggregation from the module results using the prescribed matrix and agree the basic SCR to within 0.5%.
Recompute the SCR as basic SCR plus operational risk less LACTP and LACDT and agree to the reported figure.
Recompute the risk margin using the reformed cost-of-capital rate and taper on the archived projected SCR series and the reference-date discount curve.
Recompute the linear MCR, apply the 25% and 45% bounds and the absolute floor, and confirm the binding constraint reported in S.28.01 is the one that actually binds.
testing.done: the SCR agrees within 0.5%, the risk margin recomputes on the reformed basis, and the reported MCR binding constraint is confirmed.

testing.step: Test own-funds tiering and continuous coverage of the SCR
actions: Re-perform the tiering of each own-funds instrument against its terms in the contract repository and its PRA approval, and re-apply the eligibility limits.
Confirm foreseeable dividends and distributions approved or proposed at the reference date were deducted, by agreeing to the board minutes in the board portal.
Re-perform the own funds to IFRS equity bridge and confirm every reconciling item is supported.

Test continuous coverage by reviewing the interim monitoring reports for every month in the period and confirming eligible own funds never fell below the SCR — a point-in-time pass is not the obligation.
testing.done: tiering and eligibility recompute, dividend deductions agree to board minutes, and continuous SCR coverage is evidenced month by month.

testing.step: Challenge the expert judgements and the LACDT support
actions: For each sampled expert judgement, read the recorded rationale and alternatives and form an independent view on whether the judgement remains supportable at the reference date.
Recompute the stated SCR sensitivity for the three judgements with the largest quoted impact and challenge any understated sensitivity.
Test the LACDT credit against the tax projections signed by the Tax Manager, confirming projected taxable profits are consistent with the business plan used in the ORSA.
Treat any judgement with no dated challenge in the last 12 months, or LACDT unsupported by consistent profit projections, as an exception.
testing.done: sampled judgements have an independent supportability view, recomputed sensitivities, and LACDT is tied to consistent ORSA profit projections.

testing.step: Verify model change control and permission compliance
actions: Trace every change in the model change log to an approval under the board-approved model change policy, and classify it minor or major on the policy's own criteria.
Confirm every major change was notified to or approved by the PRA before use, and that no change classified minor should on the policy criteria have been major.
Confirm the matching adjustment and TMTP permissions in force were applied only to the portfolios they cover, by tracing the MA portfolio tags in the asset file to the approval letter.
Flag any production run whose model version differs from the authorised version as a control failure regardless of the numerical impact.
testing.done: every model change traces to an approval of the right classification and the permissions were applied only within their approved scope.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the reference date, module, the difference in pounds and in coverage-ratio percentage points, and whether a submitted figure is misstated.
Assign a root cause — input data error, parameter not refreshed, unapproved model change, judgement unsupported, aggregation error, permission misapplied — and a named owner.
Where a submitted S.25 or S.28 figure is misstated beyond the resubmission threshold, open a BEEDS resubmission and a PRA notification decision with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Set a remediation date before the next reference date and carry the item into the next cycle's validation as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with quantified impact, root cause, owner, remediation date and a resubmission decision where figures are misstated.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the committee
actions: Compare the recalculation differences against the 0.5% SCR and 1% module thresholds and compute the exception count by module.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — referencing the recalculation workpapers, the change-control testing and the judgement challenge.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither built nor ran the calculation, sign and date the validation and audit workpapers.
Report the conclusion and any misstatement requiring resubmission to the Audit Committee and Board Risk Committee, and file the signed workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the 0.5%/1% thresholds and has been reported to the Audit and Board Risk Committees.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Accountable SMF for continuous monitoring of eligible own funds against the SCR, MCR and the board risk-appetite ladder for the UK entity, and for triggering the PRA notification and recovery-plan process on any breach

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Undertakings in Difficulty (immediate notification of SCR/MCR non-compliance, realistic recovery plan within 2 months and restoration within 6, short-term realistic finance scheme within 1 month and restoration within 3 for the MCR), read with Reporting 2 predefined events and the PS15/24 reporting deadlines; re-read at each annual policy refresh

In-scope processes.value: Continuous capital monitoring for the UK Solvency UK entity: daily solvency estimate -> monthly formal coverage report -> quarterly reported SCR/MCR coverage -> risk-appetite ladder trigger testing -> escalation to the Capital Management Committee, Board and the PRA, including pre-clearance of dividends and capital actions

In-scope systems.value: The solvency monitoring model rolls forward own funds and the SCR between formal valuations; market data comes from the investment platform and results are published to the capital dashboard with the ladder thresholds hard-coded

Compliance procedure documented.value: Capital Monitoring and Escalation Procedure — daily estimate method and its approximations, the four-tier risk-appetite ladder (green / amber / red / breach) with numeric coverage triggers, escalation routes and timeframes, and the recovery-plan playbook for SCR and MCR breaches

Compliance procedure approved.value: Ladder thresholds and the escalation policy approved by the Board on the Board Risk Committee's recommendation as part of the capital management policy; re-approved annually and whenever the risk appetite statement changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — daily estimate by 10:00 the next business day, monthly coverage pack to the Capital Management Committee within 10 business days of month end, quarterly reported coverage aligned to the 30-business-day submission; on breach, PRA notified immediately, recovery plan within 2 months (SCR) or finance scheme within 1 month (MCR)

Deadline reminders configured.value: The capital dashboard raises an automated amber alert to the Head of Capital Management when coverage falls below the amber trigger and a red alert to the CFO and CRO within the hour on the red trigger; on breach the GRC platform opens the recovery-plan case with the 1-month, 2-month, 3-month and 6-month statutory milestones pre-dated

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Daily estimates, monthly coverage packs, ladder trigger logs, escalation notes, committee and board minutes, PRA correspondence and recovery-plan documents retained 10 years from the period end in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every ladder trigger breach, every late escalation and every SCR/MCR non-compliance is logged with the coverage ratio at trigger, the date the trigger was hit versus the date it was escalated, and the management action taken with its outcome

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CRO signs off closure of every amber and red ladder event and confirms the management action actually restored coverage; the Board approves any recovery plan submitted to the PRA

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every daily solvency estimate, monthly coverage pack and quarterly reported coverage ratio for the UK entity in the year, plus every ladder trigger event, every capital action or dividend approved, and any period of SCR or MCR non-compliance

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on unescalated breaches — any ladder trigger not escalated within its stated timeframe, any SCR/MCR non-compliance not notified to the PRA immediately, or any dividend paid while coverage was below the red trigger, is a fail; daily estimate must track the subsequent reported ratio within 3 percentage points

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; testing is quarterly over that quarter's daily and monthly monitoring, with 100% coverage of all ladder trigger events and all capital actions in the year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Second-line reviewer outside the finance and capital management production chain, who prepared none of the monitoring packs under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly capital monitoring test workpaper (daily estimate accuracy analysis, ladder trigger reconstruction, escalation timing recomputation, dividend gate testing, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Solvency UK / capital monitoring

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Coverage ratio time series with the ladder thresholds overlaid, trigger and escalation log, board and committee minutes evidencing challenge, and any recovery plan with its milestone tracker, presentable to the PRA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Financial Officer owns the PRA capital dialogue and submits any recovery plan; the Chief Risk Officer owns risk-appetite questions; Regulatory Counsel clears any correspondence conceding a period of non-compliance before it is sent

checklist.step: Set and publish the capital risk-appetite ladder for the year
actions: Draft the four-tier ladder with numeric SCR coverage triggers — green above the target operating level, amber at the early-warning level, red at the management-action level, and breach at 100% of the SCR — plus a separate MCR coverage trigger.
Justify each trigger by reference to the ORSA stress results: the amber level should be the point at which a 1-in-10 market shock would take the firm to red.
Take the ladder to the Board Risk Committee and then the Board for approval as part of the capital management policy, and record the approving minute reference.
Publish the approved thresholds into the capital dashboard configuration and have the Head of Capital Management confirm in writing that the dashboard alerts fire at exactly those numbers.
checklist.done: a board-approved four-tier ladder with numeric SCR and MCR triggers is live in the dashboard and tied to a minute reference.

checklist.step: Build and validate the daily solvency estimate
actions: Configure the roll-forward: take the last full valuation own funds and SCR and move them for market data (yield curve, credit spreads, equity indices, FX), new business, claims and expense experience, and known capital actions.
Source the daily market data feed from the investment platform and confirm the curve used is the reference-free-rate basis consistent with the PRA published curve methodology, not a trading curve.
Document every approximation in the roll-forward — fixed sensitivities, frozen demographic assumptions, linear interpolation of the SCR — with its expected validity range.
Set the publication standard: estimated own funds, estimated SCR, estimated coverage ratio and the ladder tier, available to the CFO by 10:00 on the next business day.
checklist.done: a documented daily roll-forward publishes own funds, SCR and coverage with the ladder tier by 10:00 the next business day.

checklist.step: Run the daily monitoring and record the ladder tier
actions: Each business day open the capital dashboard, confirm the market data feed completed and the run status is green, and reject any run with a stale or partial feed.
Read the estimated SCR coverage ratio and MCR coverage ratio and record both, with the date and the ladder tier, on the monitoring log.
Where the tier has changed since the prior day, note the driver — spread widening, equity fall, curve move, capital action — with the magnitude of the market move.
Escalate a tier change to amber or worse to the Head of Capital Management the same morning, by name, not by dashboard notification alone.
checklist.done: each business day has a logged coverage ratio, ladder tier and, on any tier change, a named driver and a same-morning escalation.

checklist.step: Produce the monthly formal coverage pack
actions: Within 10 business days of month end, produce eligible own funds by tier, the estimated SCR and MCR, both coverage ratios and the ladder tier at month end and at its worst point during the month.
Include the coverage time series for the last 13 months with the ladder thresholds overlaid so trend, not just level, is visible.
Attribute the month's movement into market, experience, new business, model/assumption and capital-action components, each with a named owner for any component above 1 percentage point.
Add a forward view: projected coverage at the next two quarter ends on the plan basis and under the standard adverse scenario.
Circulate to the Capital Management Committee with the CFO, CRO, Chief Actuary and Chief Investment Officer as standing recipients.
checklist.done: a monthly pack with month-end and intra-month worst coverage, a 13-month series, attributed movement and a forward view is with the committee within 10 business days.

checklist.step: Reconcile the estimated coverage back to the reported quarterly figure
actions: When the full quarterly SCR completes, compare the reported coverage ratio to the daily estimate for the same reference date and compute the difference in percentage points.
Attribute the gap between estimate and actual to each approximation in the roll-forward — sensitivity drift, frozen assumptions, unmodelled new business mix, data timing.
Where the gap exceeds 3 percentage points, recalibrate the sensitivities used in the roll-forward and record the recalibration in the model change log.
Report the estimate-to-actual track record for the last four quarters in the monthly pack so users know how much to trust the daily number.
checklist.done: each quarter's estimate-to-actual gap is computed, attributed and, above 3 points, drives a recorded recalibration.

checklist.step: Gate every dividend, capital action and material transaction against the ladder
actions: Before any dividend, intragroup loan, share buyback, subordinated debt redemption or material reinsurance transaction, request the current and post-action pro-forma SCR and MCR coverage from the capital team.
Test the post-action coverage against the ladder: no distribution may take the firm below the amber trigger without Board approval, and none at all below red.
Confirm foreseeable dividends are deducted from own funds at the reference date once approved or proposed, and tell the Controller the date of approval.
Record the pre-action coverage, post-action pro-forma coverage, the approving body and the minute reference on the capital action register.
checklist.done: every capital action carries pre- and post-action coverage, a ladder test result and an approval minute reference on the register.

checklist.step: Escalate an amber trigger to the Capital Management Committee
actions: On the first day coverage closes below the amber trigger, notify the CFO and CRO in writing with the ratio, the driver and the distance to the red trigger.
Convene the Capital Management Committee within 5 business days with an options paper: de-risking trades, reinsurance, hedging, expense actions, suspension of distributions.
Quantify each option's effect in coverage percentage points, its cost, and its execution lead time so the committee chooses on numbers.
Record the decision, the owner and the review date on the GRC ladder-event case and set weekly monitoring until coverage recovers above amber for 10 consecutive business days.
checklist.done: an amber event has a written same-day escalation, a committee decision within 5 business days on a quantified options paper, and weekly monitoring until recovery.

checklist.step: Escalate a red trigger to the Board and prepare the management action plan
actions: On a red trigger, inform the Board Chair and the Board Risk Committee Chair the same business day and table a paper at an extraordinary meeting within 10 business days.
Present the management action plan: the specific actions, their quantified capital effect, the execution timetable, and the projected coverage path back above amber.

Assess and state whether the PRA should be informed proactively even though the SCR is not yet breached — Fundamental Rule 7 and Reporting 2 make an unreported material deterioration a separate failing.
Have the Corporate Secretary minute the board decision, the actions approved and the reporting cadence the board has demanded.
Load each approved action into the GRC case with an owner and a completion date and report progress to the board monthly until closure.
checklist.done: a red event has a same-day chair notification, a board-approved quantified action plan within 10 business days, and a recorded decision on PRA pre-notification.

checklist.step: Notify the PRA immediately on non-compliance with the SCR
actions: The moment eligible own funds fall below the SCR — or it becomes apparent this will occur in the following three months — notify the firm's named PRA supervisory contact in writing without waiting for the next reporting cycle.
State the shortfall in pounds and in coverage percentage points, the reference date and method used to establish it, the cause, and the immediate actions already taken.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the wording and confirm whether a parallel Reporting 2 predefined-event notification and an FCA notification are also owed.
Log the notification, its send timestamp and the supervisor acknowledgement in the GRC recovery case and inform the Board the same day.
checklist.done: the PRA is notified in writing immediately on SCR non-compliance with the shortfall quantified, counsel cleared and the board informed the same day.

checklist.step: Submit a realistic recovery plan within two months of the SCR breach
actions: Build the recovery plan to the Undertakings in Difficulty requirements: the measures to restore eligible own funds to the SCR level, or reduce the risk profile, within six months of the breach being observed.

For each measure state the capital effect in pounds, the counterparty or market dependency, the execution date and the evidence that it is realistic — signed term sheets, board-approved capital injections, committed reinsurance, not aspirations.
Include the projected coverage path month by month to the six-month restoration date and the sensitivity of that path to a further adverse market move.
Obtain Board approval and submit the plan to the PRA within two months of the breach, then report progress against milestones at the cadence the PRA sets.
Track the six-month restoration deadline and the possible three-month extension in the GRC case as hard dates.
checklist.done: a board-approved recovery plan with evidenced, dated measures and a monthly coverage path is with the PRA within two months of the breach.

checklist.step: Run the MCR breach path on its shorter statutory clock
actions: On non-compliance with the MCR — or where it will be breached in the following three months — notify the PRA immediately and flag that the shorter MCR timetable applies.
Prepare the short-term realistic finance scheme and submit it for PRA approval within one month of the breach being observed.
Set the plan to restore eligible basic own funds to the MCR level, or reduce the risk profile to bring the MCR back within cover, within three months.
Escalate to the Board that failure to restore within three months puts the firm's Part 4A permission at risk and record the board's instruction.
checklist.done: an MCR breach has an immediate notification, a finance scheme with the PRA within one month and a three-month restoration plan recorded at board level.

checklist.step: Reconcile intra-quarter monitoring to the reported quarterly and annual returns
actions: Agree the coverage ratio reported in the monthly pack for the quarter-end month to the S.23.01 own funds and S.25 SCR figures submitted for the same reference date.
Where the reported figure differs from the monitoring figure previously shown to the board, explain the difference in the next board pack rather than silently restating.
Confirm that any intra-quarter period of SCR or MCR non-compliance is disclosed in the annual SFCR and the Regular Supervisory Report even if coverage was restored by the reference date.
Check the quarterly submission was made within the 30-business-day solo deadline under PS15/24 and the annual within 70 business days.
checklist.done: monitoring figures reconcile to the submitted templates, differences are explained to the board, and intra-period breaches are disclosed.

checklist.step: Report capital position and ladder status to the Board each quarter
actions: Table the quarterly capital report in the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting so directors can read it: coverage ratios, ladder status, movement attribution, forward projection and open ladder events.
Ensure the paper states plainly whether the firm complied with the SCR and MCR continuously through the quarter, not just at the reference date.
Have the Corporate Secretary minute the board's challenge and any decision, including any instruction to management on capital actions or reporting cadence.
Track board actions to completion in the action log and report closure at the following meeting.
checklist.done: each quarter has a board paper circulated 5 business days ahead, a continuous-compliance statement, and minuted challenge with tracked actions.

checklist.step: Close out ladder events and confirm the action actually worked
actions: Before closing any amber or red ladder case, confirm coverage has been above the trigger for 10 consecutive business days and that the recovery is not solely a market rebound.
Test whether the management actions executed delivered the capital effect they promised, comparing forecast to realised in percentage points, and record the variance.
Where an action underdelivered, record the reason and remove it from the playbook or re-estimate its effect before it is relied on again.
Sign the closure with the date, the sustained coverage evidence and the action effectiveness assessment.
checklist.done: each ladder case is closed only on 10 days of sustained recovery, with forecast-versus-realised action effect recorded and CRO signature.

checklist.step: Retain the monitoring evidence and feed the ORSA
actions: File the daily monitoring logs, monthly packs, ladder event cases, board papers and minutes, PRA correspondence and any recovery plan under the period end with a 10-year retention label.
Summarise the year's ladder events, their drivers and the effectiveness of the actions taken for the ORSA's continuous-compliance section.
Recommend ladder threshold changes where the year's experience showed the amber trigger fired too late to leave room for action.
Confirm the archive is retrievable by date, ratio and event so a PRA request can be met inside 5 business days.
checklist.done: the monitoring record is filed with a 10-year label, feeds the ORSA continuous-compliance section, and threshold recommendations are made.

testing.step: Build the population of monitoring observations and ladder events
actions: Extract the full daily coverage ratio time series for the UK entity for the test quarter, with run status, market data timestamp and ladder tier per day.
Extract every ladder trigger event, every capital action from the capital action register, and every monthly coverage pack issued in the period.
Count business days in the period from the England and Wales calendar and confirm one monitoring observation exists per business day, listing every missing day.
Record extract parameters, dates and counts in the workpaper and have the extract owner sign completeness.
testing.done: a day-complete monitoring population with ladder events and capital actions is extracted, gaps listed, and completeness signed.

testing.step: Reconcile the monitoring series to the reported source of record
actions: Agree the quarter-end coverage ratio in the monitoring series to the SCR and own funds figures signed off by the CFO and submitted in S.23.01 and S.25.
Agree eligible own funds used in the roll-forward at the period start to the prior reference date's signed balance sheet, not to a management estimate.
Agree the market data driving the largest daily movements to independent index and curve sources rather than the firm's own feed.
Explain and document every reconciling difference above 0.5 percentage points of coverage.
testing.done: the monitoring series reconciles to the signed and submitted figures and to independent market data, with differences documented.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of monitoring days and events
actions: Take 100% of days on which the ladder tier changed, 100% of ladder trigger events and 100% of capital actions in the year.
Take 15 further business days by seeded random selection across the quarter, plus the five days with the largest single-day coverage movement.
Record the seed, the strata, the population size and the selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Include every month end so the monthly pack can be re-performed against the underlying daily data.
testing.done: a reproducible stratified sample covering all tier changes, events, capital actions, month ends and 20 further days is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the daily solvency estimate for the sampled days
actions: Rebuild the roll-forward for each sampled day from the last signed valuation, applying the day's market moves to the documented sensitivities independently of the production tool.
Compare the recomputed coverage ratio to the published estimate and quantify the difference in percentage points.
Test whether any approximation was applied outside its documented validity range — for example a linear sensitivity used through a market move several times larger than its calibration.
Flag every sampled day where the recomputation moves the ratio across a ladder threshold, since that means a trigger should have fired and did not.
testing.done: each sampled day has an independently recomputed ratio, a quantified difference, and any threshold-crossing recomputation is flagged.

testing.step: Reconstruct the ladder and recompute escalation timing
actions: Apply the board-approved ladder thresholds in force on each date to the reconstructed coverage series and derive the tier independently of the dashboard.
Compare the derived tiers to the recorded tiers and list every day where the dashboard tier was more favourable than the derived tier.

For each identified trigger, recompute elapsed time from trigger to written escalation, to committee meeting and to board notification, and test against the same-day / 5-business-day / 10-business-day standards.
Confirm the dashboard threshold configuration matches the approved policy figures by inspecting the configuration record and its change history.
testing.done: tiers are independently derived and compared, escalation intervals are recomputed against the stated standards, and dashboard configuration is verified against policy.

testing.step: Test the dividend and capital action gate
actions: For every capital action in the year, obtain the pre-action and post-action pro-forma coverage and recompute the post-action figure from the underlying own funds and SCR.
Confirm the ladder test was applied before execution and that the approving body had authority for the resulting tier under the capital management policy.
Agree the approval to the board or committee minute in the board portal and confirm the minute pre-dates the payment or execution date in the ledger.
Confirm approved or proposed dividends were deducted from own funds at the relevant reference date and did not remain in reported own funds.
testing.done: every capital action has a recomputed post-action coverage, a pre-dated approval minute at the right authority level, and correct own-funds deduction.

testing.step: Test any period of SCR or MCR non-compliance end to end
actions: Identify every day in the year on which the reconstructed coverage fell below 100% of the SCR or the MCR, using the recomputed series rather than the reported one.
For each, trace to the PRA notification and recompute elapsed time from the day the shortfall was or should have been apparent to the notification send timestamp.
Recompute the statutory clocks: two months to the recovery plan and six months to restoration for the SCR; one month to the finance scheme and three months to restoration for the MCR.
Confirm each period of non-compliance was disclosed in the SFCR and the Regular Supervisory Report even where coverage was restored before the reference date.
testing.done: every non-compliance day is identified from the recomputed series, notification and statutory clocks are recomputed, and disclosure is confirmed.

testing.step: Test governance evidence and the quality of board challenge
actions: Confirm the quarterly capital paper was posted to the board portal at least 5 business days before each meeting, using the portal's publication timestamps.
Read the minutes for each ladder event and confirm they record specific challenge and a decision, not merely that the paper was noted.
Trace every board action arising from a capital paper to its closure entry and confirm closure was evidenced, not just asserted.
Confirm the paper stated continuous compliance through the period rather than only the reference-date position.
testing.done: board papers were circulated on time, minutes evidence specific challenge and decisions, and every board action traces to evidenced closure.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the date, the coverage ratio involved, the standard missed and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause — stale market data feed, sensitivity outside validity range, dashboard threshold misconfigured, escalation not made in writing, capital action approved at the wrong level, late PRA notification — and a named owner.
Where a period of non-compliance was not notified or disclosed, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the CFO within 5 business days.
Set remediation dates before the next quarter end and carry open items into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a specific root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a self-report assessment where non-compliance went unreported.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Compute the estimate-to-actual tracking error against the 3-percentage-point standard and the escalation exception count against the zero-tolerance standard.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the reconstructed ladder, the escalation timing analysis and the capital action gate testing.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the monitoring packs and sits outside finance, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any unnotified non-compliance and open exceptions to the Audit Committee and Board Risk Committee, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the tracking-error and zero-tolerance thresholds and has been reported to both committees.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Solvency UK supervisory reporting suite for the UK entity — quarterly and annual QRTs and National Specific Templates through the Bank of England BEEDS portal, the ORSA supervisory report, the SFCR and the Regular Supervisory Report — with the CFO as the accountable SMF signatory

In-scope systems.value: The regulatory reporting engine maps the ledger, actuarial and asset data into the QRT/NST templates and produces the XBRL instance; submission is through the Bank of England BEEDS portal and the accepted instance plus receipts are filed in the financial reporting repository
