checklist.step: Build the reporting calendar and compute every due date in business days
actions: List every return owed for the UK entity by frequency: quarterly QRTs, annual QRTs, National Specific Templates, the ORSA supervisory report, the SFCR and the Regular Supervisory Report.

For each quarterly reference date compute due date = reference date + 30 business days, and for 31 December compute reference date + 70 business days, using the England and Wales bank holiday calendar under PS15/24.
Apply the PS15/24 reduced template set effective from the stated reference date and remove retired templates from the production plan rather than continuing to build them.
Publish the calendar with per-template owners and internal milestones (data cut, build, review, sign-off) and load the T-20/T-10/T-5/T-2 alerts.
Confirm with the BEEDS firm administrator that submitter accounts and permissions are active for every person on the calendar before the first cut-off.
checklist.done: a calendar exists with business-day-computed due dates, the current template set, named owners, alerts and verified BEEDS access.

checklist.step: Confirm the taxonomy version and configure the reporting engine
actions: Check the Bank of England's published XBRL taxonomy and BEEDS technical guidance for the reference date and record the taxonomy version and effective date.
Apply the vendor release implementing that taxonomy in a test environment first, and run the prior period's accepted instance through it to confirm no unintended change in template output.
Update the template inventory, entry points and validation rule set in the reporting engine and record the configuration change with an approver.
Where a template has changed, walk the mapping for each changed cell with the data owner rather than assuming the vendor mapping is right.
checklist.done: the reference-date taxonomy version is applied, regression-tested against the prior accepted instance, and mapping changes are walked with data owners.

checklist.step: Take the signed inputs from valuation, capital, investments and the ledger
actions: Collect the signed Solvency UK balance sheet, technical provisions by line of business, risk margin, SCR by module, MCR with its binding constraint, and own funds by tier from the capital and actuarial sign-off memos.
Collect the asset-by-asset holdings file for S.06.02 from the investment book of record with ISIN, CIC code, issuer, rating, valuation method and market value.
Collect premiums, claims and expenses by line of business from the ledger for S.05.01 and reinsurance data from the ceded accounting platform.
Refuse any input that is not signed and dated — an unsigned figure cannot be defended to the PRA if it is later challenged.
Record for each input the source system, extract timestamp and the signatory on the data lineage sheet.
checklist.done: every template input is a signed, dated figure with its source system, extract timestamp and signatory recorded on the lineage sheet.

checklist.step: Populate the quantitative reporting templates
actions: Run the mapping to populate the core templates: S.02.01 balance sheet, S.05.01 premiums claims and expenses, S.06.02 list of assets, S.12.01 life technical provisions, S.22.01 impact of long-term guarantee measures, S.23.01 own funds, S.25 SCR and S.28 MCR.
Populate the ring-fenced fund and matching adjustment portfolio templates separately where the firm holds MA portfolios, keeping notional SCRs unaggregated.
Complete the S.22.01 with and without the matching adjustment, the volatility adjustment and the transitional measure so the long-term guarantee impact is visible.
Check every template for unpopulated mandatory cells and for cells populated with zero where they should be blank, since the taxonomy treats them differently.
Run the internal tie-out: balance sheet totals to the ledger, own funds to the sign-off memo, SCR module lines to the capital results template.
checklist.done: all mandatory templates are populated, MA and ring-fenced portfolios are shown separately, and the internal tie-out to signed sources balances.

checklist.step: Populate the National Specific Templates
actions: Complete the NSTs required of the firm under the PRA Reporting Part, including the matching adjustment asset and cash-flow templates and the business model analysis templates where applicable.
Source the MA asset data at security level with the fundamental spread and credit quality step applied, agreeing the population to the MA portfolio tags used in the SCR calculation.
Confirm which NSTs were withdrawn under the PS15/24 template reduction and do not submit retired templates.
Reconcile every NST total that also appears in a QRT so the two sets tell the same story.
checklist.done: the applicable NSTs are complete, MA data reconciles to the SCR portfolio tags, and NST-to-QRT overlaps reconcile.

checklist.step: Generate the XBRL instance and clear the validation rules
actions: Generate the XBRL instance against the confirmed taxonomy entry point with the correct legal entity identifier, reference date, currency and reporting basis in the header.
Run the full validation rule set and resolve every blocking rule by fixing the underlying data, never by suppressing the rule.
For each non-blocking flag, write the explanation that will be given to the PRA if asked, and have the data owner confirm the figure is genuinely correct.
Run the instance through the BEEDS pre-submission validation and keep the validation report with the instance.
checklist.done: a valid instance exists with zero blocking failures, every non-blocking flag explained and owner-confirmed, and the validation report filed.

checklist.step: Run the analytical review before anyone signs
actions: Compare every material template line to the prior quarter and the prior year and flag movements above 10% or above an absolute materiality threshold.
Explain each flagged movement with a named business driver from the movement analysis — new business volume, market moves, assumption changes, reinsurance transactions — and a named owner.
Cross-check the story between templates: a technical provision movement in S.12.01 must be visible in S.02.01 and consistent with the SCR life module movement in S.25.
Challenge any explanation of 'data correction' by tracing it to a logged issue and confirming whether the prior period is therefore misstated.
checklist.done: every flagged movement has a named driver and owner, inter-template consistency is checked, and data corrections are traced to logged issues.

checklist.step: Obtain sign-off through the approval matrix before submission
actions: Review the submission pack: templates, analytical review, validation report with non-blocking explanations, data lineage sheet and the list of open reporting issues.
Confirm the Chief Actuary has signed the technical provisions and SCR inputs and the Controller has signed the ledger-sourced lines.
Sign as the accountable SMF, dating the signature before the submission timestamp — a sign-off dated after the fact is a control failure regardless of intent.
Record the sign-off in the sign-off matrix with names, roles, dates and the exact template versions approved.
checklist.done: a complete sign-off matrix exists with SMF, actuarial and ledger signatures all dated before submission.

checklist.step: Submit through the Bank of England BEEDS portal and capture the receipt
actions: Log in to the BEEDS portal, select the correct firm, return type and reference period, and upload the signed XBRL instance.
Wait for the processing result rather than closing the session — an upload is not a submission until BEEDS returns acceptance.
Where BEEDS rejects the instance, read the rule reference, fix the underlying data, re-obtain sign-off if a signed figure changed, and resubmit before the deadline.
Save the BEEDS submission receipt, reference number, timestamp and acceptance message as a PDF into the financial reporting repository next to the submitted instance.
Record the submission date against the calendar entry and compute the business days used against the 30 or 70 business day allowance.
checklist.done: BEEDS acceptance is obtained and evidenced with reference number and timestamp, and business days used against the deadline are recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the ORSA supervisory report within two weeks of the assessment concluding
actions: Take the board-approved ORSA supervisory report from the Risk Management team with the date the board concluded the assessment recorded on it.
Compute the due date as the board conclusion date plus two weeks under PRA Rulebook Reporting 2 and load it as a hard deadline.
Submit through BEEDS as the ORSA return type, confirm acceptance and file the receipt with the board minute reference attached.
Where the ORSA was triggered by a significant change in risk profile rather than the annual cycle, state that trigger in the covering note.
checklist.done: the ORSA supervisory report is accepted by BEEDS within two weeks of the board conclusion date, with the minute reference filed.

checklist.step: Produce the SFCR and the Regular Supervisory Report on the PS3/24 basis
actions: Draft the SFCR to the prescribed structure — business and performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation for solvency purposes, capital management — using the accepted annual QRT figures as the only source for quantitative statements.
Apply the PS3/24 split: the policyholder-facing SFCR content and the supervisor-only Regular Supervisory Report content, ensuring nothing supervisor-only leaks into the public document.
Attach the public disclosure QRTs required to accompany the SFCR and tie every number in the narrative to a template cell.
Have the external auditor confirm the audit of the relevant SFCR elements is complete and attach the audit opinion.
Obtain Board approval of the SFCR before publication and record the approving minute.
checklist.done: an audited, board-approved SFCR and a separate RSR exist, with every narrative figure tied to an accepted QRT cell.

checklist.step: Publish the SFCR and file the RSR with the supervisor
actions: Publish the SFCR on the firm's website at the location previously notified to the PRA, and capture a dated screenshot and the URL as evidence of the publication date.
Submit the Regular Supervisory Report through BEEDS and file the receipt.
Notify the PRA supervisory contact of the publication with the URL, and confirm the document remains accessible for the required period rather than being rotated off the site.
File the published PDF, the screenshot, the URL and the receipts in the financial reporting repository under the reference date.
checklist.done: the SFCR is published with dated evidence of the URL and date, the RSR is accepted by BEEDS, and both are filed.

checklist.step: Handle resubmissions and restatements under a controlled process
actions: On discovering an error in an accepted submission, quantify the misstatement per template cell in pounds and against the resubmission materiality threshold in the reporting policy.
Decide resubmit now, correct in the next cycle, or no action, and record the decision, the threshold applied and the approver — the CFO approves every resubmission.
Where the error affects a reported coverage ratio or a figure already published in the SFCR, notify the PRA supervisory contact before resubmitting.
Log the issue with root cause, the control that failed, an owner and a fix date, and confirm the fix is in place before the next reference date.
checklist.done: each error has a quantified impact, a CFO-approved disposition, PRA pre-notification where a published figure changes, and a logged root-cause fix.

checklist.step: Answer PRA data queries within the agreed window
actions: Log every PRA query on a submitted template with the date received, the template and cell in question and the response deadline the supervisor set.
Trace the queried cell back through the lineage sheet to the source extract and the signed input, and answer with the underlying figure and its source, not a restatement of the template.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager review, and Regulatory Counsel clear, any response that concedes an error before it is sent.
File the query, the response and any follow-up in the financial reporting repository against the reference date.
checklist.done: each PRA query is logged, answered from traced source data within the supervisor's deadline, and filed with its response.

checklist.step: Archive the submission and run the post-cycle control review
actions: Archive the submitted instance, source extracts, mapping documentation, validation reports, sign-off matrix, BEEDS receipts and PRA correspondence under the reference date with a 10-year retention label.
Compute the cycle metrics — business days used against the allowance, blocking failures encountered, late inputs by owner, resubmissions — and table them at the reporting control review.
Agree fixes for every input that arrived late or unsigned, naming the upstream owner, and carry them into the next cycle's plan.
Confirm the archive is retrievable by reference date, template and cell so a PRA request can be met inside 5 business days.
checklist.done: the cycle is archived with a 10-year label and a control review with cycle metrics and named upstream fixes has been held.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions and resubmissions for the year
actions: List every Solvency UK return owed by the UK entity for the year from the PRA Reporting Part template inventory and the firm's reporting calendar.
Extract from BEEDS records every submission and resubmission made, with return type, reference date, submission timestamp and acceptance status.
Match owed to submitted and list every return owed with no accepted submission, and every submission with no corresponding calendar entry.
Record the extract date, source and counts, and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager sign the population as complete.
testing.done: an owed-versus-submitted population is built from BEEDS records, gaps are listed, and completeness is signed.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted template values to the signed source of record
actions: Take the accepted annual XBRL instance and agree S.23.01 own funds, S.25 SCR and S.28 MCR to the CFO-signed capital sign-off memo cell by cell.
Agree S.02.01 balance sheet lines to the general ledger trial balance and the Solvency UK balance sheet, and S.12.01 technical provisions to the Chief Actuary's signed valuation results.
Agree S.06.02 total asset market value and holding count to the investment book of record extract used in the SCR calculation.
Treat any difference above 0.5% of the line, or any difference at all in own funds and SCR, as an exception requiring root cause.
testing.done: key template lines agree to signed capital, actuarial, ledger and investment sources within the stated tolerance.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of submissions and template cells
actions: Take 100% of the annual submission, the SFCR, the RSR, the ORSA supervisory report, and every resubmission and late filing in the year.
Take one quarterly pack by seeded random selection and record the seed and selection date.
Within the selected packs take 30 template cells stratified by value, covering at least five templates and including every cell that carried a non-blocking validation flag.
Document the strata and rationale so the sample is reproducible by a third party.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering the annual pack, one quarter, all resubmissions and 30 stratified cells is documented.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory deadline and the days actually used
actions: Recompute each quarterly due date as reference date plus 30 business days and each annual as reference date plus 70 business days using the England and Wales bank holiday calendar, independent of the firm's calendar tool.
Recompute the ORSA supervisory report deadline as the board conclusion date plus two weeks, taking the conclusion date from the board minute rather than the report cover.
Compare each recomputed due date to the BEEDS acceptance timestamp — acceptance, not upload — and quantify any lateness in business days.
Test the firm's calendar configuration for holiday and weekend handling by re-deriving three due dates and comparing to the tool's output.
testing.done: every deadline is independently recomputed against BEEDS acceptance timestamps and any lateness is quantified in business days.

testing.step: Re-perform the XBRL and validation controls
actions: Confirm the taxonomy version and entry point in the accepted instance header match the version the Bank of England required for that reference date.
Re-run the validation rule set against the accepted instance and confirm zero blocking failures and that every non-blocking flag has a filed, owner-confirmed explanation.
Confirm the entity identifier, reference date, currency and reporting basis in the header are correct for the submitting entity.
Test that no validation rule was suppressed or overridden by inspecting the reporting engine configuration change history for the cycle.
testing.done: taxonomy, header and validation results are verified on the accepted instance and no rule suppression is evidenced in the configuration history.

testing.step: Trace sampled cells through the lineage to source and identifiers
actions: For each of the 30 sampled cells, follow the lineage sheet from the template cell to the mapping rule, to the source extract, to the source system record.
Confirm the source extract carries the signatory and timestamp recorded on the lineage sheet and that the extract file still hashes to the archived value.
For asset-level cells confirm the ISIN, CIC code and rating in S.06.02 agree to the investment book of record for the same holding.
Flag any cell whose lineage is broken, undocumented, or resolves only to a manual journal or an adjustment spreadsheet with no owner.
testing.done: each sampled cell traces to a signed, hash-verified source record with matching identifiers, or the broken lineage is logged.

testing.step: Test sign-off, authority and timing
actions: For each sampled submission, open the sign-off matrix and confirm the SMF, actuarial and ledger signatures are present with names, roles and dates.
Confirm every signature date precedes the BEEDS submission timestamp and that the version approved is the version submitted, by comparing template version references.
Confirm the signatory held the relevant Senior Management Function at the signature date by reference to the firm's SMF register.
Confirm SFCR publication was board-approved before the publication date recorded in the dated website screenshot.
testing.done: sign-offs are present, correctly authorised, version-matched and dated before submission, and SFCR board approval pre-dates publication.

testing.step: Test resubmissions, restatements and SFCR consistency
actions: For every resubmission, recompute the misstatement per cell and confirm the resubmission threshold in the reporting policy was applied correctly and the CFO approved the disposition.
Confirm the PRA was pre-notified where a resubmission changed a reported coverage ratio or a figure already published in the SFCR.
Trace every quantitative statement in the published SFCR narrative back to a cell in the accepted annual instance and flag any figure that does not tie.
Confirm the external audit opinion covers the SFCR elements required to be audited and is attached to the published document.
testing.done: resubmissions are threshold-tested and CFO-approved, PRA pre-notification is evidenced, and every SFCR figure ties to an accepted template cell.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the return, reference date, template and cell, the value misstated or the deadline missed, and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause — late or unsigned upstream input, mapping not updated for the taxonomy change, manual adjustment outside the lineage, sign-off obtained after submission, deadline miscomputed — and a named owner.
For any missed statutory deadline or unnotified restatement, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the CFO within 5 business days.
Set remediation dates before the next reference date and carry open items into the next cycle's testing as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with cell-level detail, root cause, owner, remediation date and a self-report assessment where a deadline or restatement was unreported.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Compute the exception rate by return and compare it to the zero-missed-deadline and zero-unsigned-submission thresholds and the 0.5% cell tolerance.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the deadline recomputation, the cell tracing and the sign-off testing.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, reviewed or signed none of the submissions, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any late filings and any unnotified restatement to the Audit Committee and the Board, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the deadline, sign-off and 0.5% tolerances and has been reported to the Audit Committee and Board.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual ORSA process for the UK entity — the assessment of overall solvency needs, continuous compliance with the SCR, MCR and technical provisions, and the deviation of the risk profile from standard formula assumptions — and presents it to the Board for approval before the supervisory report is filed

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 3 (own risk and solvency assessment, its three required assessments and the requirement to perform it at least annually and after any significant change in risk profile) read with Reporting 2 for the ORSA supervisory report; both re-read at the start of each ORSA cycle and the dated extracts filed with the ORSA record

In-scope processes.value: Annual ORSA for the UK Solvency UK entity: risk profile refresh -> overall solvency needs assessment on the firm's own basis -> forward-looking projection of own funds, SCR and MCR over the business plan horizon -> stress, scenario and reverse stress testing -> standard formula appropriateness assessment -> board challenge and approval -> supervisory report; plus the off-cycle trigger process

In-scope systems.value: The risk register, risk appetite metrics and control assessments feed the ORSA from the GRC platform; projections are run in the capital and planning models and the approved ORSA record and supervisory report are held in the board portal and the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: ORSA Policy and Process Manual — governance and timetable, the three required assessments and how each is evidenced, the overall solvency needs methodology, stress and reverse stress design, the off-cycle significant-change triggers, and the board approval and filing route

Compliance procedure approved.value: ORSA Policy approved by the Board on the Board Risk Committee's recommendation; reviewed annually, and re-approved on any change to the risk appetite statement, the business plan horizon or the PRA's ORSA expectations

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: At least annually, plus within the cycle following any significant change in risk profile; the ORSA supervisory report must reach the PRA within two weeks of the board concluding the assessment under PRA Rulebook Reporting 2, so the board approval date is the deadline driver, not the year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: The ORSA timetable in the GRC platform alerts owners at each milestone — risk profile refresh, projection run, stress results, draft to Board Risk Committee, board approval, filing — and the board approval date automatically opens a two-week filing task assigned to the Regulatory Reporting Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The ORSA record — risk profile assessment, overall solvency needs workings, projection runs, stress and reverse stress results, standard formula appropriateness analysis, board papers, minutes and the filed supervisory report with its BEEDS receipt — retained 10 years from the board approval date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed off-cycle triggers, unaddressed board challenges, late filing of the supervisory report and material errors in the projections are logged as ORSA process issues with root cause, owner and a dated remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CEO confirms management's ownership of the ORSA conclusions and the actions arising; the Board approves the ORSA itself and the Chief Risk Officer signs the closure of every ORSA action

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The annual ORSA record for the UK entity, every off-cycle ORSA or significant-change assessment performed or declined during the year, every ORSA action raised, and the supervisory report as filed with its BEEDS receipt

Pass/fail thresholds.value: All three Conditions Governing Business 3 assessments must be evidenced or the ORSA fails; filing later than two weeks after board conclusion is a fail; any significant-change trigger met without a documented decision, or any board challenge with no traceable response, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is at least annual and event-triggered; testing runs annually over the completed ORSA cycle, with 100% coverage of off-cycle triggers met during the year and of board challenges raised

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Third-line review independent of the risk function that authored the ORSA; no reviewer may have drafted any section of the ORSA record under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ORSA assurance workpaper (assessment-by-assessment evidence mapping, projection recalculation, trigger testing, board challenge tracing, filing timing recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Solvency UK / ORSA

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The ORSA record, the supervisory report as filed, board papers and minutes evidencing challenge, the projection and stress workings, and the action tracker, producible to the PRA within 5 business days of request

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer owns PRA questions on the ORSA and the risk profile; the Chief Actuary answers projection and technical provision method challenge; the Chief Executive Officer fronts any supervisory meeting on the firm's own view of solvency needs

checklist.step: Open the ORSA cycle and set the timetable against the board calendar
actions: Set the cycle milestones backwards from the board meeting at which approval will be sought: risk profile refresh, projection run, stress results, Board Risk Committee review, board approval, and filing within two weeks of approval.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that the target board meeting has ORSA approval on its agenda and that papers are due 5 business days beforehand.

Name an owner for each ORSA section — risk profile, overall solvency needs, projections, stresses, standard formula appropriateness, capital management plan — and confirm each owner's availability against the timetable.
Load the milestones into the GRC platform so slippage is visible rather than discovered at the board meeting.
checklist.done: a milestone timetable tied to the board approval date exists with a named owner per ORSA section and alerts loaded in GRC.

checklist.step: Refresh the risk profile from the risk register and the year's experience
actions: Extract the current risk register with inherent and residual ratings, control effectiveness ratings and the risk owner for every principal risk of the UK entity.

Overlay the year's actual experience: operational loss events, incidents notified to the PRA, longevity and mortality experience variance, credit downgrades and defaults, expense overruns and complaint volumes.

Identify risks that are material to the firm but not captured, or captured only partially, in the standard formula — for example longevity concentration, matching adjustment portfolio risk, sponsor covenant risk, climate transition and physical risk, and cyber.
Run risk owner workshops to re-rate the principal risks and record the rationale for every change in rating.
Produce a ranked risk profile with a written statement of the five risks that most drive the firm's own view of its solvency needs.
checklist.done: a re-rated, ranked risk profile exists supported by the year's loss and experience data, naming the risks not fully captured by the standard formula.

checklist.step: Assess overall solvency needs on the firm's own basis
actions: Define the firm's own risk measure and confidence level for the overall solvency needs assessment and state explicitly where it differs from the 99.5% one-year VaR of the SCR.

Quantify capital for each principal risk on that own basis, including the risks the standard formula does not cover, and aggregate with the firm's own diversification view rather than the prescribed matrix.
Add the buffers the board considers necessary — model uncertainty, business plan execution, an operational risk allowance calibrated to the firm's own loss history.
Present the overall solvency needs figure alongside the SCR and explain the gap risk by risk, since that gap is the heart of the first Conditions Governing Business 3 assessment.
Have the Chief Actuary review the quantification method and record the challenge and its resolution.
checklist.done: an overall solvency needs figure exists on a stated own basis, reconciled risk by risk to the SCR, with actuarial challenge recorded.

checklist.step: Project own funds, SCR and MCR across the business plan horizon
actions: Take the board-approved business plan — new business volumes and mix, expense budget, investment strategy, reinsurance programme, dividend policy — as the base case, and confirm with the FP&A Manager that no unapproved variant is being used.
Project own funds, the SCR, the MCR and both coverage ratios for each year of the plan horizon, showing the coverage path against the risk appetite ladder.
Model the planned capital and risk management actions explicitly, with the date each is assumed to occur, so the projection does not rely on unstated management action.
Confirm the projection assumptions on longevity, expenses and investment return are the same as those used in the valuation and pricing bases, and explain any deliberate difference.
Show the projected risk margin on the reformed cost-of-capital basis so the plan reflects the current regime rather than the pre-reform position.
checklist.done: a plan-horizon projection of own funds, SCR, MCR and coverage exists on the board-approved plan with dated management actions and assumptions tied to the valuation basis.

checklist.step: Assess continuous compliance with capital requirements and technical provisions
actions: Assess whether the firm will comply with the SCR and MCR continuously across the plan horizon, not merely at each year end, using the intra-year coverage monitoring evidence from the year just passed as the test of that claim.

Assess compliance with the requirements on technical provisions: data quality, method appropriateness, assumption setting and the validity of the matching adjustment and transitional measure permissions across the horizon.
Identify any point in the projection where coverage approaches the risk appetite amber trigger and state the management action that would be taken and by whom.

Record this as an explicit, separately evidenced assessment — it is the second of the three Conditions Governing Business 3 assessments and is the one most often merged into the projection narrative and thereby lost.
checklist.done: a separately evidenced continuous-compliance assessment covers the SCR, MCR and technical provision requirements across the horizon with named actions at pressure points.

checklist.step: Assess the deviation of the risk profile from the standard formula assumptions
actions: Work through each standard formula module and compare its calibration assumptions to the firm's actual exposure — for an annuity writer, longevity concentration, illiquid and privately placed assets, matching adjustment portfolio behaviour and counterparty concentration are the usual divergences.
Quantify the effect of each material deviation, stating whether the standard formula over- or understates the risk and by how much.

Conclude explicitly whether the standard formula remains appropriate to the firm's risk profile, and if not, what the firm intends to do — undertaking-specific parameters, a partial internal model application, or a capital add-on discussion with the PRA.
Record this as the third Conditions Governing Business 3 assessment with its own conclusion, not as an appendix.
Have the Model Risk Manager provide second-line challenge on the quantification and record the outcome.
checklist.done: each material deviation from standard formula assumptions is quantified with a direction and an explicit appropriateness conclusion, second-line challenged.

checklist.step: Design and run the ORSA stress and scenario suite
actions: Design single-factor stresses calibrated to the firm's own risk profile — longevity improvement shock, credit spread widening with downgrades, interest rate fall, expense inflation, mass lapse on the deferred book.
Design at least two combined scenarios with a coherent narrative and a timeline, such as a stagflation scenario combining spread widening, downgrade migration and expense inflation over 18 months.

Run each stress through the projection model and report the coverage path, the point of maximum stress and the management actions assumed, separating actions the board has pre-approved from those that would need a fresh decision.
Report results in coverage percentage points against the risk appetite ladder so the board can see which stresses take the firm to amber, red or breach.
checklist.done: single and combined stresses are run on the projection with coverage paths, maximum stress points and management actions separated into pre-approved and new.

checklist.step: Run the reverse stress test to the point of business model failure
actions: Define failure for this firm — inability to meet the SCR with no credible recovery, or loss of the matching adjustment permission, or a funding position that makes the annuity book unsaleable.

Work backwards to identify the combinations of events that would produce it, including non-financial paths such as a systemic ICT failure, a mass mis-selling finding or the failure of a material outsourcer.
Assess the plausibility of each path and record the early-warning indicators that would show it developing, mapping each to a metric already monitored.
Present the reverse stress results to the Board Risk Committee as a discussion item, since their value is in the challenge they provoke rather than the number they produce.
checklist.done: failure is defined for this firm, the paths to it are identified with plausibility and mapped early-warning indicators, and the committee has discussed them.

checklist.step: Draw the ORSA conclusions and set the capital management plan
actions: State the ORSA conclusions plainly: the overall solvency needs figure, whether current and projected resources meet it, whether the standard formula remains appropriate, and the risks that most threaten the plan.
Set the capital management plan for the horizon — target operating coverage level, dividend capacity, planned issuance or redemption of subordinated debt, and the reinsurance actions relied on.
Raise a specific, owned and dated action for every conclusion that requires management response, and load them into the GRC action tracker.
Have the Chief Executive Officer confirm management's ownership of the conclusions before the paper goes to the Board.
checklist.done: written conclusions, a capital management plan and dated owned actions exist, with CEO confirmation of management ownership.

checklist.step: Take the ORSA through Board Risk Committee challenge
actions: Post the draft ORSA to the board portal at least 5 business days before the Board Risk Committee meeting, with a two-page summary of conclusions and the questions management wants tested.
Run the committee session so that challenge is directed at the assumptions and the stress design, not the presentation, and capture every challenge verbatim on the challenge log.
Assign each challenge to a named owner with a response date before the board approval meeting.
Update the ORSA for the responses and show the committee what changed, since an unchanged document after real challenge is itself a finding.
checklist.done: committee challenge is logged verbatim with owners and response dates, and the ORSA shows what changed in response.

checklist.step: Obtain Board approval and record the conclusion date
actions: Table the final ORSA for Board approval with the committee's recommendation and the challenge log attached.

Minute the board's discussion, the approval decision and any instruction to management, recording the exact date the board concluded the assessment — this date starts the two-week filing clock under Reporting 2.
Record director attendance and any dissent, since the ORSA is a board-owned document and the PRA reads the minutes as evidence of engagement.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager of the conclusion date the same day and open the filing task.
checklist.done: a minuted board approval exists with the conclusion date recorded and the two-week filing task opened the same day.

checklist.step: File the ORSA supervisory report with the PRA within two weeks
actions: Prepare the supervisory report from the approved ORSA record, covering the three required assessments, the methods and assumptions used, the stress results and the conclusions.
Compute the due date as the board conclusion date plus two weeks and submit through the Bank of England BEEDS portal as the ORSA return type.
Confirm BEEDS acceptance rather than upload, and file the receipt, reference number and timestamp with the board minute reference.
Where the ORSA was triggered off-cycle by a significant change in risk profile, state the trigger and its date in the covering note.
checklist.done: the supervisory report is accepted by BEEDS within two weeks of board conclusion with the receipt filed against the minute reference.

checklist.step: Embed the ORSA in decision-making rather than filing and forgetting it
actions: Require the ORSA conclusions to be cited in the papers supporting the next material decisions — new product approval, reinsurance renewal, investment strategy change, dividend proposal.
Set the target operating coverage level from the ORSA as the standing constraint used by the Capital Management Committee.
Report ORSA action progress at each Board Risk Committee sitting until the actions close.
Where a decision departs from an ORSA conclusion, require the paper to say so explicitly and explain why.
checklist.done: ORSA conclusions are cited in subsequent decision papers, set the operating coverage constraint, and departures are explicitly explained.

checklist.step: Monitor the off-cycle triggers for a significant change in risk profile
actions: Maintain the defined trigger list: a material acquisition or bulk annuity transaction, a change of investment strategy, loss or variation of the matching adjustment permission, a major reinsurance restructure, a red ladder event, or a material model or assumption change.
Review the triggers monthly at the Risk Committee against actual events and record a decision — ORSA required or not required — with reasons, every time a trigger is met.
Where an off-cycle ORSA is required, run a scoped assessment covering the affected risks and take it through the same board approval and two-week filing route.
Log a 'not required' decision with the reasoning so the judgement is auditable rather than invisible.
checklist.done: triggers are reviewed monthly with a recorded reasoned decision each time one is met, and off-cycle ORSAs follow the same approval and filing route.

checklist.step: Archive the ORSA record and close the cycle
actions: Archive the complete ORSA record — risk profile, overall solvency needs workings, projections, stress and reverse stress results, standard formula analysis, board papers, challenge log, minutes, supervisory report and BEEDS receipt — under the board approval date.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm retrieval by approval date, assessment and risk.
Hold a cycle retrospective with the section owners and record what to change next year — data gaps, late inputs, stresses that produced no insight.
Carry every open ORSA action into the tracker with its owner and date so the next cycle starts from a known position.
checklist.done: a complete, indexed ORSA record is archived for 10 years, a retrospective is recorded, and open actions are carried forward with owners.

testing.step: Build the population of ORSA outputs, triggers and actions
actions: Assemble the complete ORSA record for the cycle and list its sections against the ORSA Policy's required contents, flagging any section absent.
Extract every significant-change trigger event from the GRC platform, the capital ladder event log and the board minutes for the year, whether or not an off-cycle ORSA followed.
Extract every ORSA action raised in the current and prior cycle with its owner, due date and status.
Extract the board and committee challenge logs and record the population counts and extract date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the ORSA record, trigger events, actions and challenge logs are assembled with counts documented and missing sections flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile the ORSA inputs to the signed sources of record
actions: Agree the opening own funds, SCR and MCR in the projection to the CFO-signed capital sign-off memo for the reference date.
Agree the business plan volumes, expenses and dividend assumptions in the projection to the board-approved plan in the board portal, not to a working version.
Agree the risk register extract used for the risk profile to the register as it stood at the assessment date, using the GRC audit trail.
List and explain every difference, treating any use of an unapproved plan variant as an exception.
testing.done: projection and risk profile inputs reconcile to the signed capital memo, the board-approved plan and the point-in-time risk register.

testing.step: Map evidence to each of the three required assessments
actions: Take PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 3 and list its three required assessments — overall solvency needs, continuous compliance with capital requirements and technical provisions, and deviation of the risk profile from standard formula assumptions.
For each, identify the specific section, page and workings in the ORSA record that constitute the assessment and its conclusion.
Reject as insufficient any assessment evidenced only by narrative assertion with no underlying quantification or conclusion.
Record a pass or fail per assessment — a missing or unevidenced assessment fails the ORSA regardless of the quality of the rest.
testing.done: each of the three required assessments is mapped to specific quantified evidence and a conclusion, with a pass or fail recorded.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of projections, stresses and judgements
actions: Take 100% of the base case projection, the reverse stress test and the standard formula appropriateness analysis.
Take 5 stress scenarios by seeded random selection from the suite, plus the two producing the largest coverage deterioration.
Take 8 key assumptions and management actions relied on in the projection, weighted to those with the largest quantified effect.
Record the seed, strata and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of projections, stresses and weighted assumptions is documented with seed and strata.

testing.step: Re-perform the projection and stress calculations
actions: Re-run the base case projection from the archived model version and inputs and compare year-by-year own funds, SCR and coverage to the reported figures.
Re-run the sampled stresses applying the documented shock definitions and compare the coverage deterioration in percentage points to the reported result.
Test whether management actions credited in the projection were separated into pre-approved and requiring-new-decision, and remove any unapproved action to see whether the conclusion survives.
Flag any stress whose reported result cannot be reproduced from the archived inputs as an exception regardless of direction.
testing.done: base case and sampled stresses are reproduced from archived inputs, and the conclusion is retested with unapproved management actions removed.

testing.step: Test the standard formula appropriateness analysis independently
actions: Take each standard formula module and independently identify where the firm's exposure diverges from the module's calibration, without reading the firm's analysis first.

Compare your list to the firm's and treat any material divergence the firm did not identify — longevity concentration, illiquid asset behaviour, matching adjustment portfolio risk, climate transition risk — as an exception.
Recompute the quantified effect of the two largest identified deviations and compare to the firm's figures.
Test whether the stated appropriateness conclusion actually follows from the quantified deviations or contradicts them.
testing.done: an independent deviation list is compared to the firm's, the two largest effects are recomputed, and the appropriateness conclusion is tested for internal consistency.

testing.step: Trace board challenge to a documented response
actions: Confirm from portal publication timestamps that the draft ORSA reached the Board Risk Committee and the Board at least 5 business days before each meeting.
Take every challenge in the committee and board minutes and trace it to a named owner, a dated response and, where the challenge required it, a change in the ORSA document.
Compare the version approved by the board to the version originally tabled and confirm the changes correspond to the challenges raised.
Treat any challenge with no traceable response, or an unchanged document after substantive challenge, as an exception.
testing.done: every minuted challenge traces to an owner, a dated response and a corresponding document change where required.

testing.step: Recompute the filing clock and test the off-cycle triggers
actions: Take the board conclusion date from the minute, not the report cover, add two weeks and compare to the BEEDS acceptance timestamp for the ORSA supervisory report.
Confirm the filed supervisory report content matches the board-approved ORSA record on the conclusions, the overall solvency needs figure and the stress results.
For every significant-change trigger event in the year, confirm a dated, reasoned ORSA-required or not-required decision exists and test the reasoning against the ORSA Policy trigger definitions.
Where an off-cycle ORSA was performed, recompute its own two-week filing clock from its board conclusion date.
testing.done: the filing clock is recomputed against BEEDS acceptance, filed content matches the approved record, and every trigger has a reasoned dated decision.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the assessment or section affected, what the ORSA Policy or Conditions Governing Business 3 required, and what was actually evidenced.

Assign a root cause — assessment merged into narrative and lost, unapproved plan variant used, management action credited without approval, trigger not reviewed, challenge not tracked, filing clock started from the wrong date — and a named owner.
Where the supervisory report was filed late or its content diverges from the approved record, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the CRO within 5 business days.
Set remediation dates inside the next ORSA cycle and carry the items into next year's assurance as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue tied to the specific requirement, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a self-report assessment where filing failed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Board
actions: Assess the result against the stated thresholds: all three assessments evidenced, filing within two weeks, every trigger decided, every challenge tracked.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the assessment evidence mapping, the projection re-performance and the challenge tracing.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted no section of the ORSA, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any failed assessment to the Audit Committee and the Board, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the three-assessment and two-week thresholds and has been reported to the Audit Committee and Board.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual stress and scenario testing programme for the UK entity jointly with the Chief Risk Officer — the ORSA stress suite, reverse stress testing, climate scenario analysis and any Bank of England industry-wide insurance stress test submission

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business (ORSA stress and reverse stress testing) and the Reporting Part as amended by PS15/24 for the return of stressed and sensitivity information in the QRTs and NSTs, read with PS3/24 for the sensitivity disclosures in the SFCR and Regular Supervisory Report; plus the Bank of England's published scenario specification for any industry exercise in the year

In-scope processes.value: Annual stress and scenario testing for the UK Solvency UK annuity and life business: scenario design and calibration -> model and data preparation -> stressed valuation and SCR runs -> management action assessment -> reverse stress testing -> climate scenario analysis -> board review -> feed into the ORSA, the capital management plan and the SFCR sensitivities

In-scope systems.value: Stressed runs are executed in the valuation and capital model on the archived reference-date model points; asset stresses are sourced from the investment platform and results are published through the reporting layer into the ORSA and board packs

Compliance procedure documented.value: Stress and Scenario Testing Framework — scenario library with calibrations and their evidence base, severity standards (1-in-10 and 1-in-20 equivalents), the rules on crediting management actions, reverse stress methodology, climate scenario methodology and the run control and documentation standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Framework approved by the Board Risk Committee and the scenario suite for each cycle approved by the Board before the runs are executed; the framework is reviewed annually and after any Bank of England scenario publication that changes market practice

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — the stress suite must complete in time for the ORSA board approval date, the resulting sensitivities must be in the SFCR and Regular Supervisory Report for the 70 business day annual cycle under PS15/24, and any Bank of England insurance stress test submission runs to the deadline published in that exercise's specification

Deadline reminders configured.value: The stress testing plan sets milestones back from the ORSA board date — scenario approval, data lock, run completion, results review, board paper — with alerts to the scenario owners; any Bank of England exercise deadline is loaded as a separate hard date with T-30, T-15 and T-5 business day alerts

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Scenario specifications with calibration evidence, the locked model version and input data, run logs, stressed results by scenario, the management action assessment, board papers and minutes retained 10 years from the reference date in the model governance repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Scenarios not run, runs executed on an unapproved model version, management actions credited without approval, results that cannot be reproduced and late submissions to an industry exercise are logged with root cause, owner and a dated fix

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CRO signs the stress results as fit for board and ORSA use and closes every finding from the independent review of the stress programme

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every scenario in the approved suite for the cycle — single-factor stresses, combined scenarios, reverse stress paths, climate scenarios and any Bank of England exercise scenario — together with their run logs, results and the management actions credited in each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every board-approved scenario must be run and reproducible from archived inputs; independent re-performance must agree the stressed coverage ratio within 1 percentage point; any scenario omitted, any unapproved management action credited, or any calibration with no evidence base is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with off-cycle runs on a significant change in risk profile; testing runs annually over the completed suite with 100% coverage of the reverse stress test, the climate scenarios and any industry exercise submission

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Second-line model risk review independent of the actuarial team that designed and ran the scenarios, supported by Internal Audit; no reviewer may have calibrated or executed a scenario under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual stress testing validation workpaper (scenario inventory and completeness check, calibration challenge, re-performed runs, management action testing, reproducibility results, exceptions) in the model governance repository, cross-linked to the ORSA record

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Scenario specifications with calibration evidence, stressed result packs, management action assessment, reverse stress analysis and the board minutes evidencing challenge, producible to the PRA within 5 business days and directly reusable in a Bank of England stress test submission

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Actuary answers PRA and Bank of England questions on calibration and method; the Chief Risk Officer owns questions on scenario selection and management actions; the CFO owns any question about the capital consequences of the results

checklist.step: Set the scenario suite for the cycle and get it approved before any run
actions: Take the ranked risk profile from the ORSA process and select scenarios that actually target the firm's dominant risks — for an annuity writer, longevity improvement, credit spread widening with downgrade migration, interest rate falls and expense inflation.
Check whether the Bank of England has published an insurance stress test specification for the year and, if so, add its prescribed scenarios and timetable to the suite unchanged.
Retire scenarios that produced no decision-relevant insight last cycle and record why, rather than carrying the library forward untouched.
Present the suite with its severity standards to the Board Risk Committee for approval and record the approving minute reference before any run is executed.
checklist.done: a board-committee-approved scenario suite exists with a minute reference, targeting the ranked risks and incorporating any Bank of England exercise scenarios.

checklist.step: Calibrate each scenario and evidence the severity claimed
actions: For each single-factor stress state the shock precisely — basis points of spread widening by credit quality step, percentage fall in the interest rate curve by term, percentage uplift to mortality improvement rates, percentage point addition to expense inflation.

Evidence the severity with a named source: historical episode, published index data, the standard formula calibration as a benchmark, or the firm's own experience distribution, and state the return period claimed.

Confirm each combined scenario is internally coherent — spreads widening while risk-free rates fall while expense inflation rises needs a narrative that holds together, not three unrelated shocks stacked.
Record the calibration and its evidence on the scenario specification sheet and have the Chief Actuary approve it before the run.
checklist.done: every scenario has a precise shock definition, a named evidence source, a stated return period and Chief Actuary approval of the calibration.

checklist.step: Lock the model, data and baseline the stresses will run against
actions: Identify the reference-date baseline: the signed own funds, SCR, MCR and technical provisions, and confirm the stresses will run against that baseline and not a later management estimate.
Lock the model version and parameter set to the authorised production version and record the version identifier on every scenario run request.
Lock the input data extracts — policy, asset and reinsurance files — with their hashes so every scenario runs on the same starting position.
Re-run the baseline through the locked configuration and confirm it reproduces the signed results before any stressed run is started.
checklist.done: the baseline reproduces from the locked model version and hashed inputs, and the version identifier is recorded against every scenario.

checklist.step: Run the market and credit stresses
actions: Apply the spread-widening shock by credit quality step to the asset portfolio, including the downgrade migration assumption, and revalue the matching adjustment portfolios with the fundamental spread recalculated on the post-downgrade ratings.
Apply the interest rate scenarios to assets and liabilities simultaneously and report the net effect, since an annuity book's exposure is the mismatch not the level.
Apply equity, property and currency shocks to the non-matching assets and to any shareholder funds held outside the MA portfolios.
Report for each scenario the effect on own funds, the SCR, the risk margin and the coverage ratio, and state whether the MA portfolio would still pass its eligibility tests under the stress.
Escalate immediately any scenario in which the matching adjustment would be lost, because that is a step change rather than a gradual deterioration.
checklist.done: market and credit scenarios are run with MA revaluation and eligibility retested, and MA-loss scenarios are escalated on discovery.

checklist.step: Run the demographic and expense stresses
actions: Apply the longevity improvement shock by uplifting the CMI improvement parameters and the base table adjustment, and report the effect on best estimate liability, risk margin, SCR and coverage.
Apply the expense inflation shock across maintenance and overhead expense assumptions for the full run-off, not just the plan horizon, since annuity liabilities carry decades of expense.
Apply the mass and level lapse stresses to any deferred or unit-linked business and confirm the direction of the loss for each block.
Compare each stressed result to the corresponding standard formula module capital to show whether the standard formula would have covered the event.
checklist.done: demographic and expense scenarios are run over full run-off with results compared to the corresponding standard formula module capital.

checklist.step: Run the combined scenarios with a coherent timeline
actions: Run each combined scenario over its stated timeline — for example spread widening and downgrades in months 1 to 6, expense inflation building over 18 months — rather than as a single instantaneous shock.
Report the coverage path quarter by quarter, identify the point of maximum stress, and state how long the firm remains below each risk appetite ladder tier.
Track the second-order effects: downgrades increasing the counterparty default module, MA fundamental spread increases reducing the benefit, and the risk margin moving with the SCR.
Present each combined scenario with a one-page narrative that a non-actuarial director can follow from cause to capital consequence.
checklist.done: combined scenarios are run over a timeline with a quarter-by-quarter coverage path, maximum stress point, second-order effects and a plain narrative.

checklist.step: Assess management actions honestly and separate the approved from the aspirational
actions: List every management action credited in the stressed results with its assumed capital effect, execution date and the market conditions it depends on.
Classify each as pre-approved by the Board with documented capacity, feasible but requiring a new decision, or aspirational, and state the classification alongside the result.

Test whether the action remains executable in the scenario itself — a de-risking trade assumed in a stressed market, or a reinsurance transaction assumed when the reinsurance market has hardened, is not automatically available.
Report every scenario twice: pre-management-action and post-management-action coverage, so the board sees the raw exposure before the mitigation.
Where a scenario is only survivable on aspirational actions, say so explicitly in the board paper.
checklist.done: every credited action is classified and feasibility-tested in-scenario, and results are reported both pre- and post-management-action.

checklist.step: Run the reverse stress test back from failure
actions: Define the failure point for this firm — breach of the SCR with no credible recovery, loss of the matching adjustment permission, or an unfundable annuity payroll — and agree it with the Board Risk Committee before running.
Solve backwards for the shock magnitudes that reach it, running the model iteratively, and record the combination for each path.
Include non-financial paths — a prolonged ICT failure, a material outsourcer collapse, a systemic mis-selling finding — assessing them qualitatively where the model cannot quantify them.
Assess the plausibility of each path against history and current conditions, and map early-warning indicators to metrics the firm already monitors so the paths are watchable rather than theoretical.
checklist.done: failure is defined and agreed, the shock combinations reaching it are solved and recorded, and each path has a plausibility view and mapped early-warning indicators.

checklist.step: Run the climate scenario analysis
actions: Run at least an early transition, a late disorderly transition and a hot-house physical risk pathway over a long horizon consistent with the liability duration.

For transition risk, apply sector-level asset repricing to the credit portfolio using the carbon intensity and transition readiness data held on the holdings, and report the effect on own funds and the MA fundamental spread.
For physical risk, assess the effect on mortality and morbidity assumptions and on property and infrastructure holdings.
Report the results with an explicit statement of the data gaps and proxies used, since climate analysis carries far more uncertainty than the financial stresses and hiding that is itself a finding.
Feed the conclusions to the Chief Investment Officer for the investment strategy review and into the ORSA risk profile.
checklist.done: transition and physical pathways are run over a liability-consistent horizon with data gaps stated and conclusions fed to investments and the ORSA.

checklist.step: Complete any Bank of England industry-wide stress test submission
actions: Read the exercise specification in full and build a requirements matrix of every prescribed scenario, template and qualitative question with its owner and internal due date.

Run the prescribed scenarios exactly as specified without substituting the firm's own calibration, and document any approximation used with its justification, since the Bank compares firms on a common basis.
Complete the qualitative questionnaire consistently with the quantitative submission — inconsistency between the two is the most commonly raised finding.
Obtain the sign-off the specification requires, submit through the channel it names by the published deadline, and file the receipt.
Record the firm's results against any published aggregate so outlier positions can be explained before the Bank asks.
checklist.done: the exercise is submitted complete and on the published deadline with prescribed calibrations unaltered, approximations documented and the receipt filed.

checklist.step: Produce the results pack and the sensitivities for disclosure
actions: Build the results pack: one row per scenario showing baseline and stressed own funds, SCR, coverage ratio, the movement in percentage points, and the ladder tier reached.
Rank the scenarios by coverage deterioration so the board sees immediately which risks matter most.
Extract the sensitivity disclosures required for the SFCR and Regular Supervisory Report and hand them to the Statutory Reporting Manager tied to the accepted annual template figures.
Cross-check that every number in the pack traces to a specific archived run identifier.
checklist.done: a ranked results pack exists with every figure traceable to an archived run identifier, and the SFCR sensitivities are handed over tied to submitted figures.

checklist.step: Take the results to the Board Risk Committee and the Board
actions: Post the results pack and scenario narratives 5 business days before the meeting with a summary naming the three scenarios that take the firm furthest down the ladder.
Direct the committee's challenge at severity — whether the calibrations are hard enough — and at the credibility of the management actions, not at presentation.
Capture every challenge with a named owner and a response date, and record whether the board asked for additional scenarios to be run.
Minute the board's conclusion on whether the firm's risk profile and capital resources remain within appetite in light of the results.
checklist.done: the board has challenged severity and management action credibility on a pack circulated 5 days ahead, with challenges owned and the conclusion minuted.

checklist.step: Convert the results into decisions and actions
actions: Use the results to set or reset the target operating coverage level and the risk appetite ladder triggers for the coming year.
Raise a specific action for every scenario that breaches appetite — hedging, reinsurance, de-risking, expense reduction, product design change — with an owner, a capital effect and a date.
Feed the results into the ORSA, the capital management plan, the investment strategy review and the reinsurance renewal brief so the analysis drives decisions rather than sitting in a pack.
Track the actions in the GRC platform and report progress to the Board Risk Committee until closure.
checklist.done: appetite triggers are reset where needed and every appetite-breaching scenario has an owned, dated action tracked in GRC.

checklist.step: Run off-cycle stresses when the risk profile or the market changes materially
actions: Define the triggers for an off-cycle run: a large bulk annuity transaction, a change of investment strategy, a market dislocation, a material assumption change, or a red ladder event.
On any trigger, run the affected scenarios within 10 business days against the latest available baseline and report to the Capital Management Committee.
Record the trigger, the decision to run or not run with reasons, and the results, so the judgement is auditable.
Where the off-cycle result changes the ORSA conclusions, tell the Chief Risk Officer so the significant-change ORSA trigger can be assessed.
checklist.done: each trigger has a dated reasoned decision, off-cycle runs complete within 10 business days, and ORSA impact is escalated where conclusions change.

checklist.step: Archive the runs and close the cycle
actions: Archive per scenario: the specification with calibration evidence, model version, input hashes, run log, output files, management action assessment and the results pack entry.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm each scenario is retrievable by cycle, scenario name and run identifier.
Hold the cycle retrospective and record which scenarios drove a decision, which produced nothing, and what data limitations constrained the analysis.
Carry the retrospective conclusions into next cycle's suite design so the library evolves with the risk profile.
checklist.done: every scenario is archived with its calibration, version and hashes under a 10-year label, and the retrospective feeds next cycle's suite design.

testing.step: Build the population of scenarios approved, run and reported
actions: Take the board-approved scenario suite from the Board Risk Committee minute and list every scenario approved for the cycle.
Extract from the model governance repository every stress run executed in the cycle with its scenario name, model version, input hash, run date and operator.
Extract the results pack and the scenario list disclosed in the ORSA and, where applicable, the Bank of England exercise submission.
Match approved to run to reported and list every scenario approved but not run, run but not reported, and reported but not approved.
testing.done: an approved-run-reported matching exists with every mismatch listed and the extract parameters documented.

testing.step: Reconcile the stress baseline to the signed source of record
actions: Agree the baseline own funds, SCR, MCR and technical provisions used in the runs to the CFO-signed capital sign-off memo for the reference date.
Re-verify the archived input file hashes against the files the runs consumed and confirm all scenarios ran on the same locked data.
Confirm the model version recorded on each run matches the authorised production version in the model change log for that date.
Treat any run against an unauthorised version, a later management estimate or an unhashed input as an exception regardless of the result.
testing.done: the baseline agrees to the signed memo, input hashes verify, and every run traces to the authorised model version.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of scenarios to re-perform
actions: Take 100% of the reverse stress test, the climate scenarios and any Bank of England exercise scenario.
Take 6 further scenarios by seeded random selection, plus the three producing the largest coverage deterioration.
Take 10 calibration parameters weighted toward those driving the largest results, and 10 management actions credited across the suite.
Record the seed, strata, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering the mandatory scenarios, 9 further scenarios and 10 weighted calibrations and actions is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled scenario runs from archived inputs
actions: Re-execute each sampled scenario from the archived model version, parameter set and hashed input files, applying the shock exactly as written on the specification sheet.
Compare the recomputed stressed own funds, SCR and coverage ratio to the reported figures and quantify the difference in percentage points.

Test the shock was applied as specified — for spread stresses confirm the credit quality step mapping and the fundamental spread recalculation; for longevity confirm the improvement parameter uplift, not just a base table change.
Flag any scenario differing by more than 1 percentage point of coverage, or that cannot be reproduced at all, as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled scenario is re-executed from archived inputs and agrees within 1 percentage point, or the failure to reproduce is logged.

testing.step: Challenge the calibrations and the severity claimed
actions: For each sampled calibration read the stated evidence source and independently verify the figure against it — the historical episode, the published index series, or the firm's own experience data.

Compare the claimed return period to the standard formula calibration for the same risk and flag any scenario claiming 1-in-20 severity that is milder than the standard formula's 1-in-200 sub-module by an implausible margin.
Test coherence of the combined scenarios: confirm the shocks assumed together are consistent with the stated narrative and with observed correlations in stressed periods.
Treat any calibration with no named evidence source, or an unexplained softening against last cycle, as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled calibration is verified against its named source, severity is benchmarked and combined-scenario coherence is tested.

testing.step: Test the management actions credited in the results
actions: For each sampled management action, trace the claimed pre-approval to a board or committee minute in the board portal and confirm the documented capacity covers the amount credited.
Test in-scenario feasibility: for a de-risking trade confirm market liquidity would plausibly exist under the stress; for reinsurance confirm the capacity assumption survives a hardened market.
Recompute the stressed coverage with unapproved and infeasible actions removed and compare it to the reported post-action figure.
Confirm results were reported both pre- and post-management-action to the board, since a post-action-only presentation hides the raw exposure.
testing.done: each sampled action is traced to approved capacity and feasibility-tested, and coverage is recomputed with unsupported actions stripped out.

testing.step: Test the reverse stress test and the climate analysis for substance
actions: Confirm the failure definition was agreed with the Board Risk Committee before the run and is genuinely a failure point rather than a mild appetite breach.
Re-solve one reverse stress path from the archived model and confirm the recorded shock combination does reach the defined failure point.
Confirm non-financial failure paths were considered and are not limited to market shocks, and that each path has mapped early-warning indicators tied to metrics actually monitored.
For the climate analysis, confirm transition and physical pathways were run over a horizon consistent with liability duration and that data gaps and proxies are stated rather than concealed.
testing.done: the failure definition is pre-agreed and material, one path is re-solved to failure, non-financial paths and indicators exist, and climate data gaps are disclosed.

testing.step: Trace results into the ORSA, the disclosures and any industry submission
actions: Agree the stress results quoted in the ORSA record and the board paper to the archived run outputs by run identifier.
Agree the sensitivities disclosed in the SFCR and the Regular Supervisory Report to the same runs and to the accepted annual template figures.

For any Bank of England exercise, confirm the prescribed calibrations were applied unchanged, that every prescribed template and qualitative question was answered, and that the submission was accepted by the published deadline.
Flag any figure quoted externally that does not tie to an archived run as an exception.
testing.done: every externally quoted stress figure ties by run identifier to an archived run, and any industry submission is confirmed complete, unaltered and on time.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the scenario, the standard missed and the effect on the reported coverage or on the board's understanding.

Assign a root cause — scenario approved but not run, calibration unevidenced or softened, unapproved model version used, management action credited without capacity, result not reproducible, prescribed calibration altered — and a named owner.
Where a figure disclosed in the SFCR or submitted to the Bank of England is affected, escalate to the CFO for a correction and disclosure decision within 5 business days.
Set remediation dates before the next cycle's scenario approval and carry the items into next year's validation as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with scenario-level detail, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a disclosure decision where external figures are affected.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Assess the result against the thresholds: every approved scenario run, re-performance within 1 percentage point, no unapproved management action credited, every calibration evidenced.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the re-performance results, the calibration challenge and the management action testing.
Have the independent reviewer, who calibrated and executed no scenario in the suite, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any misstated external figure to the Audit Committee and Board Risk Committee, and file the signed workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the completeness, 1-point re-performance and calibration-evidence thresholds and has been reported to both committees.
